Financial Services Industry & Retail Con.q: What must firms do when a retail client is categorised as a professional client on request?

Financial Services Industry & Retail Con.w: Firms must assess whether the client meets the legal tests for elective professional status before re-categorising them.

n.3: Disclosure duties remain, though scope may differ.

Financial Services Industry & Retail Con.q: What must firms do if product complexity prevents average consumers from understanding key risks?

n.1: Disclaimers alone are insufficient.
n.2: Firms must still act to ensure understanding.
n.3: Execution-only does not remove communication duties.

Financial Services Industry & Retail Con.q: What is a key obligation when designing financial promotions?
Financial Services Industry & Retail Con.w: Promotions must present a balanced picture of risks and rewards so consumers are not misled.

n.0: Benefits-only messaging would mislead.
n.1: Costs must be disclosed, not excluded.
n.3: Technical-only language obscures clarity.

Financial Services Industry & Retail Con.q: What obligation applies to firms when providing advice to retail clients?
Financial Services Industry & Retail Con.w: Advised recommendations must be suitable, considering the client's objectives, financial situation and risk tolerance.

n.0: Growth cannot be guaranteed.
n.1: Cheapest is not always suitable.
n.3: Advice must fit the client, not mirror competitors.

Financial Services Industry & Retail Con.q: What is a typical long-term goal requiring disciplined saving?
Financial Services Industry & Retail Con.w: Home ownership requires disciplined saving over time, often for a deposit, a long-term financial priority.

n.1: Groceries are a short-term, recurring cost.
n.2: Utility bills are ongoing, not a saving goal.
n.3: Leisure costs are discretionary, not structured.

Financial Services Industry & Retail Con.q: Which client type receives the highest level of protection under COBS?
Financial Services Industry & Retail Con.w: Retail clients receive the highest protection because they are treated as the least experienced and knowledgeable.

n.0: Professional clients have lower protection.
n.1: Eligible counterparties receive the least protection.
n.2: Institutional investors are treated as professional.

Financial Services Industry & Retail Con.q: What is the primary goal of retirement saving?
o: Avoiding the need for estate planning
Ensuring adequate income in later life
Financial Services Industry & Retail Con.w: Retirement saving provides income in later life once earnings cease, maintaining living standards.

n.0: Liquidity risk is met by emergency savings.
n.1: Estate planning is still needed.
n.3: Inheritance may still be taxed.

Financial Services Industry & Retail Con.q: When providing investment advice, what must suitability assessments take into account?
Financial Services Industry & Retail Con.w: Suitability assessments must weigh the client's objectives, financial situation and risk profile so recommendations fit their needs.

n.0: Marketing channels are irrelevant to suitability.
n.1: Competitor performance is not a client-specific factor.
n.2: Sales targets cannot override client needs.

Financial Services Industry & Retail Con.q: What obligation applies when firms handle client assets under CASS?
Financial Services Industry & Retail Con.w: CASS requires firms to segregate and protect client assets so they stay safe if the firm fails.

n.1: Using assets to fund operations breaches safeguarding.
n.2: Automatic proprietary investment misuses assets.
n.3: Client ownership must be preserved, not transferred.

Financial Services Industry & Retail Con.q: Why must firms disclose total costs including ongoing service fees?
o: So firms can reduce FCA levies
Financial Services Industry & Retail Con.w: Total cost disclosure lets consumers evaluate whether a product offers fair value relative to its benefits.

n.0: Levies are not affected by disclosure.
n.1: SM&CR accountability continues regardless.
n.2: Disclosure aids comparison, it does not exclude rivals.

Financial Services Industry & Retail Con.q: Which need is met through establishing an emergency fund?
o: Access to cash in unforeseen situations
Financial Services Industry & Retail Con.w: Emergency funds provide liquidity for unexpected costs such as job loss or medical bills, without borrowing.

n.1: Emergency funds focus on liquidity, not growth.
n.2: Taxation is unrelated to emergency savings.
n.3: Luxury spending is not the purpose of the fund.

Financial Services Industry & Retail Con.q: Why is protection insurance often prioritised for households with dependants?
o: It provides income if the earner dies
It removes the need for budgeting
It replaces the need for retirement savings
Financial Services Industry & Retail Con.w: Protection policies ensure dependants are financially supported if the main earner dies or becomes critically ill.

n.0: Insurance manages risk; it does not guarantee returns.
n.2: Budgeting is still needed even with cover.
n.3: Retirement saving remains a separate long-term need.

Financial Services Industry & Retail Con.q: Why must financial promotions be clear, fair and not misleading?
Financial Services Industry & Retail Con.w: Promotions must let consumers understand features, risks and costs so they can make informed decisions.

n.1: Driving sales is not the regulatory objective.
n.2: HMRC record rules concern tax, not promotion clarity.
n.3: The FSCS concerns compensation, not promotions.

Financial Services Industry & Retail Con.q: Why must firms provide disclosures on inducements received from product providers?
o: To let firms bypass suitability rules
To ensure only in-house products sell
Financial Services Industry & Retail Con.w: Disclosing inducements ensures transparency so clients know of potential conflicts that could influence advice.

n.0: Remuneration is not eliminated, only disclosed.
n.1: Suitability rules apply regardless of disclosure.
n.2: Advice must be impartial, not steered in-house.

Financial Services Industry & Retail Con.q: How do pensions help meet long-term consumer needs?
o: By removing all underlying investment risk
Financial Services Industry & Retail Con.w: Pensions let individuals accumulate savings tax-efficiently to provide income in retirement.

n.0: Pensions are long-term, not for daily liquidity.
n.1: Pensions diversify but do not remove risk.
n.3: Emergency funds are separate and remain accessible.

Financial Services Industry & Retail Con.q: How must a distributor act when MI shows harm in a defined target market subgroup?
Financial Services Industry & Retail Con.w: Distributors must notify the manufacturer and adjust distribution or communications to mitigate harm to affected consumers.

n.0: Waiting for complaints is reactive, not compliant.
n.2: Price cuts alone may not fix a targeting mismatch.
n.3: Switching without consent breaches consumer rights.

Financial Services Industry & Retail Con.q: What must firms ensure about remuneration structures under the FCA's rules?
o: They guarantee a fixed sale commission
Financial Services Industry & Retail Con.w: Remuneration policies must avoid conflicts that drive unsuitable recommendations, ensuring fair treatment of consumers.

n.0: Fixed per-sale commission risks bias and is not required.
n.1: Cross-selling is not a regulatory objective.
n.2: Rewarding volume alone risks poor outcomes.

Financial Services Industry & Retail Con.q: When a firm designs a new investment product, what must it identify under product governance rules?
o: A way to limit FCA oversight
Financial Services Industry & Retail Con.w: Manufacturers must identify a defined target market so products meet the needs and characteristics of intended consumers.

n.1: Commission strategy is not the regulatory focus.
n.2: FCA oversight cannot be avoided by authorised firms.
n.3: Cheapest channels may not suit the target market.

Financial Services Industry & Retail Con.q: What should firms provide when offering execution-only services?
Financial Services Industry & Retail Con.w: For complex products, execution-only sales need an appropriateness test to check clients understand the risks.

n.1: Execution-only excludes full financial planning.
n.2: Suitability monitoring applies to advice, not execution-only.
n.3: Outcomes cannot be guaranteed.

Financial Services Industry & Retail Con.q: Why must firms disclose the risks of early encashment on investment products?
Financial Services Industry & Retail Con.w: Firms must disclose risks such as capital loss or surrender penalties so clients can make informed choices.

n.0: Supervision does not change with product exit terms.
n.2: Returns are not guaranteed; risks are highlighted.
n.3: Charges are not eliminated by disclosure.

Financial Services Industry & Retail Con.q: Why is budgeting considered a foundational financial need?
o: It exempts consumers from all tax reporting
It prevents all forms of financial risk
It directs income to key priorities
Financial Services Industry & Retail Con.w: Budgeting ensures income is allocated across spending, debt, saving and protection in line with priorities.

n.0: Budgeting does not guarantee investment returns.
n.1: Tax reporting obligations remain regardless.
n.2: Budgeting reduces but cannot prevent all risk.

Financial Services Industry & Retail Con.q: Which product is most suitable for building an emergency fund?
Financial Services Industry & Retail Con.w: An instant access savings account offers liquidity and safety, making it the most suitable vehicle for emergencies.

n.0: Corporate bonds tie up capital and carry credit risk.
n.1: Private equity is illiquid and unsuitable short-term.
n.3: Life assurance is protection, not accessible cash.

Financial Services Industry & Retail Con.q: What is the main purpose of the Consumer Understanding outcome?
o: Allow advisers to skip suitability reports
Financial Services Industry & Retail Con.w: The Consumer Understanding outcome makes firms give clients information they can understand to make effective decisions.

n.0: Capital growth is not guaranteed.
n.1: Disclosure remains mandatory.
n.3: Suitability reports are still required for advice.

Financial Services Industry & Retail Con.q: What financial need is met by income protection insurance?
Financial Services Industry & Retail Con.w: Income protection provides regular payments when a consumer cannot work due to illness or disability.

n.0: It replaces income, not provides investment returns.
n.1: It is for essential stability, not luxury spending.
n.3: FCA oversight continues regardless of cover.

Financial Services Industry & Retail Con.q: Which need is directly met by establishing a household budget?
o: Guaranteeing a reduction in inheritance tax
Financial Services Industry & Retail Con.w: Budgeting controls spending and allocates income to priorities such as debt, saving and insurance.

n.0: Budgeting does not directly affect inheritance tax.
n.1: Capital growth comes from investing, not budgeting.
n.2: Emergency funds are still needed alongside budgeting.

Financial Services Industry & Retail Con.q: What is the primary financial need addressed by life assurance?
Financial Services Industry & Retail Con.w: Life assurance ensures dependants receive financial support on the policyholder's death, protecting household stability.

n.1: Life assurance is not a guaranteed-growth investment.
n.2: Emergency needs require liquid savings, not assurance.
n.3: Budgeting is still needed alongside cover.

Financial Services Industry & Retail Con.q: Why do many plans prioritise life assurance for parents with young children?
o: To replace pensions as the main savings tool
To exempt families from inheritance tax
To secure dependants if a parent dies
Financial Services Industry & Retail Con.w: Life assurance provides a lump sum or income if a parent dies, keeping the household financially secure.

n.0: Life assurance is protection, not a savings substitute.
n.1: It is not an investment product for profit.
n.2: Inheritance tax may still apply.

Financial Services Industry & Retail Con.q: What is a key reason for prioritising saving for children's education?
o: It exempts parents from FCA rules
It guarantees a higher salary for the child
It prepares for predictable future costs
Financial Services Industry & Retail Con.w: Education savings help families meet foreseeable expenses, avoiding future borrowing or financial stress.

n.0: FCA rules govern firms, not family saving.
n.1: Inheritance tax is unaffected by education saving.
n.2: Saving cannot guarantee a child's future salary.

Financial Services Industry & Retail Con.q: Why might liquidity be prioritised before long-term investing?
o: To meet emergencies without selling investments
To avoid paying any income tax
Financial Services Industry & Retail Con.w: Liquidity lets consumers meet short-term emergencies without disturbing long-term investments, supporting stability.

n.1: Liquidity planning does not remove tax obligations.
n.2: Immediate consumption can harm financial resilience.
n.3: Liquidity is about access to cash, not returns.

Financial Advice Legal Concepts & Consid.q: Which statute governs trustee powers and duties in England and Wales?
Financial Advice Legal Concepts & Consid.w: The Trustee Act 2000 modernised trustee powers, including investment duties and the delegation of functions.

n.0: The Wills Act governs the formalities of wills.
n.1: The Law of Property Act covers property rights.
n.3: The Companies Act governs corporate law.

Financial Advice Legal Concepts & Consid.q: A bankruptcy order is made but no insolvency practitioner is appointed. Which official handles the case initially?
Financial Advice Legal Concepts & Consid.w: The Official Receiver, a civil servant, initially administers bankruptcies and liquidations before an insolvency practitioner may be appointed.

n.0: Judges make bankruptcy orders but do not manage estates.
n.1: Directors cannot manage a bankruptcy estate.
n.3: The Treasury Solicitor is not responsible for insolvency estates.

Financial Advice Legal Concepts & Consid.q: Under the Contracts (Rights of Third Parties) Act 1999, what is the effect on someone who is not a party to a contract?
o: They are prevented from enforcing any contractual right
They may enforce all consumer contracts as a regulator
They are freed from providing consideration in contracts
They may enforce terms that expressly benefit them
Financial Advice Legal Concepts & Consid.w: The Act creates exceptions to privity, allowing identified third parties to enforce contractual terms made for their benefit.

n.0: The Act grants, rather than removes, third-party rights.
n.1: Regulators enforce legislation, not contracts under this Act.
n.2: Consideration remains necessary; the Act does not remove it.

Financial Advice Legal Concepts & Consid.q: Which statute sets out the intestacy rules in England and Wales?
o: The Inheritance (Provision for Family and Dependants) Act 1975
Financial Advice Legal Concepts & Consid.w: The Administration of Estates Act 1925 sets out the intestacy rules, determining how estates are distributed without a will.

n.0: The Trustee Act modernises trustee powers, not intestacy.
n.1: The Law of Property Act governs property rights.
n.2: The 1975 Act allows dependants to claim provision.

Financial Advice Legal Concepts & Consid.q: Which condition must be satisfied for a deed, such as a trust deed, to be valid under English law?
o: It must be registered at Companies House
It must be signed, witnessed and delivered
It must be signed only by the donor
It requires consideration from both parties
Financial Advice Legal Concepts & Consid.w: A deed must be in writing, signed, witnessed and delivered, and needs no consideration unlike a simple contract.

n.0: Companies House registration applies only to certain documents.
n.2: A donor's signature alone, without witnessing, is insufficient.
n.3: Deeds do not require consideration to bind.

Financial Advice Legal Concepts & Consid.q: Which best describes ownership under a trust arrangement?
o: Beneficiaries hold both legal and equitable title
The settlor keeps legal ownership after creating it
Trustees hold legal title; beneficiaries the equitable
The trust itself is a legal person owning assets
Financial Advice Legal Concepts & Consid.w: Trust law splits ownership: trustees hold legal title while beneficiaries enjoy the equitable interest.

n.0: Beneficiaries do not hold legal title.
n.1: The settlor usually gives up legal ownership.
n.3: A trust is not itself a legal person.

Financial Advice Legal Concepts & Consid.q: Spouses Anna and Ben hold their home as joint tenants. Which feature applies on one spouse's death?
o: The survivor takes the whole by survivorship
The deceased's share passes under their will
Each owns a fixed share sold separately
The title converts to tenants in common
Financial Advice Legal Concepts & Consid.w: Joint tenancy carries the right of survivorship: the deceased's interest ends and the survivor takes the whole.

n.1: Under joint tenancy the interest passes by survivorship, not by will.
n.2: Fixed shares are a feature of tenants in common.
n.3: Conversion needs severance; it is not automatic on death.

Financial Advice Legal Concepts & Consid.q: What is the main legal effect of severing a joint tenancy?
o: It transfers the property to a third party
It voids the original purchase contract
It becomes a tenancy in common
Financial Advice Legal Concepts & Consid.w: Severance removes the right of survivorship, creating a tenancy in common so each party can leave their share by will.

n.0: Severance changes the form of co-ownership, not ending it.
n.1: Severance does not transfer to third parties.
n.2: The purchase contract stays valid.

Financial Advice Legal Concepts & Consid.q: Two floating charges are created over the same company assets at different times. Which rule generally determines priority?
o: The later charge always takes precedence
Overlapping charges are treated as invalid
Priority is decided by a shareholder vote
First in time ranks first unless postponed
Financial Advice Legal Concepts & Consid.w: Generally the first floating charge registered has priority, unless a later chargeholder gains priority by agreement or statute.

n.0: Later charges take priority only if agreed or by statute.
n.1: Overlapping charges are valid unless prohibited.
n.2: Shareholders have no role in deciding priority.

Financial Advice Legal Concepts & Consid.q: Which restriction typically applies to an individual who has been made bankrupt?
o: They cannot be a company director without leave

They must permanently cease all financial activity
Financial Advice Legal Concepts & Consid.w: A bankrupt is prohibited from acting as a company director or being involved in company management without the court's approval.

n.2: Bankruptcy does not remove voting rights.
n.3: Restrictions are lifted on discharge, not permanent.

Financial Advice Legal Concepts & Consid.q: A bankruptcy order is made against an individual. Which legal effect follows immediately?
o: The debtor immediately regains full solvency
Control of assets passes to the trustee in bankruptcy
All of the debtor's debts are automatically cancelled
The debtor may freely dispose of their property

n.2: Debts are addressed through the process, not simply cancelled.
n.3: The bankrupt loses control of property that vests in the trustee.

Financial Advice Legal Concepts & Consid.q: A client divorced last year but has not updated her will. What is the effect of the divorce on gifts to her ex-spouse?
o: The entire will is revoked automatically

The former spouse's entitlement is simply halved
They are treated as if the ex-spouse had died

Financial Advice Legal Concepts & Consid.q: Which doctrine prevents a person who unlawfully caused another’s death from inheriting from them?

n.0: Pari passu applies to insolvency distributions.
n.1: Survivorship passes property to survivors of joint ownership.

o: Each owns the whole property jointly
Ownership automatically transfers to the survivor
Each owns a distinct definable share
Neither may transfer their share independently
Financial Advice Legal Concepts & Consid.w: Tenants in common each hold a separate, definable share that may be disposed of by will or sale.

Financial Advice Legal Concepts & Consid.q: A person who witnessed a will is also left a gift in it. What is the effect?

Financial Advice Legal Concepts & Consid.q: A borrower wants a new company substituted into an existing loan contract in place of the original lender. Which mechanism achieves this?

Financial Advice Legal Concepts & Consid.q: Which factor distinguishes real property from personal property?

Financial Advice Legal Concepts & Consid.q: What term describes what remains of an estate after debts, taxes and specific gifts are settled?

Financial Advice Legal Concepts & Consid.q: A newly bankrupt client asks which of her debts will be written off. Which of the following is discharged by bankruptcy?

Financial Advice Legal Concepts & Consid.q: What is the main role of an executor named in a will?

Financial Advice Legal Concepts & Consid.q: A director deliberately conceals company assets during insolvency. Which statutory offence does this amount to?

Financial Advice Legal Concepts & Consid.q: Which type of charge must be registered at Companies House to be valid against a liquidator?

Financial Advice Legal Concepts & Consid.q: A man dies without leaving a valid will. How are his assets distributed?

Equally among all his friends and relatives
At the discretion of the local authority
Under the statutory rules of intestacy

Financial Advice Legal Concepts & Consid.q: Which statement best describes consideration in a simple, non-deed contract for an investment service?
o: Only the client must provide consideration

Financial Advice Legal Concepts & Consid.q: Which equitable remedy lets courts enforce an informal trust arrangement to achieve fairness?

Financial Advice Legal Concepts & Consid.q: A woman dies intestate leaving a spouse and children. Under intestacy rules, what does the spouse receive?

Financial Advice Legal Concepts & Consid.q: Which document typically evidences ownership of shares in a company?

Financial Advice Legal Concepts & Consid.q: Which UK process lets a small company obtain a moratorium while it considers a rescue plan?

Financial Advice Legal Concepts & Consid.w: A small company may apply for a CVA with a moratorium, giving protection from creditor action while proposals are considered.

Financial Advice Legal Concepts & Consid.q: Once a company's insolvency is likely, which statutory duty requires its directors to act in the interests of creditors?

The duty to declare interests in transactions
The duty to avoid wrongful trading

Financial Advice Legal Concepts & Consid.q: A beneficiary’s spouse acts as a witness to a will. What is the legal effect under the Wills Act?

Financial Advice Legal Concepts & Consid.q: An adviser transfers a client's service agreement to a new provider. Which statement distinguishes assignment from novation?

Novation transfers only rights, whereas assignment transfers obligations

Financial Advice Legal Concepts & Consid.w: Assignment passes rights, such as to payment, but not burdens; novation substitutes a party, transferring both rights and obligations with tri-party consent.

n.0: Assignment does not transfer obligations automatically.
n.1: Assignment usually needs no debtor consent; novation needs all parties'.
n.2: This inverts the position; novation moves both, assignment rights only.

Financial Advice Legal Concepts & Consid.q: Which principle applies where one party relies on another's promise without formal consideration?
Financial Advice Legal Concepts & Consid.w: Promissory estoppel stops a party going back on a promise the other has reasonably relied upon, even without consideration.

n.0: Ratification approves an agent's unauthorised act.
n.2: Frustration concerns supervening impossibility.
n.3: Privity determines who may enforce a contract.

Financial Advice Legal Concepts & Consid.q: Which type of power of attorney automatically ceases if the donor loses mental capacity?
o: A general power registered with the OPG
Financial Advice Legal Concepts & Consid.w: An ordinary power of attorney is valid only while the donor has capacity and ends automatically if capacity is lost.

n.1: A lasting power continues after capacity is lost, once registered.
n.2: Enduring powers also survive loss of capacity if registered.
n.3: OPG registration does not make an ordinary power endure.

Financial Advice Legal Concepts & Consid.q: A client owns a home with their partner as joint tenants and then dies intestate. How does their share pass?
o: Divided under intestacy among all the heirs
To the administrator of the estate
Sold with the proceeds divided by the court
Financial Advice Legal Concepts & Consid.w: Property held as joint tenants passes automatically by survivorship to the surviving co-owner, outside the intestacy rules.

n.1: Intestacy does not apply to joint tenancy property.
n.2: Administrators do not take joint tenancy property.
n.3: Survivorship applies, so there is no court-ordered sale.

Financial Advice Legal Concepts & Consid.q: In a company insolvency, which of the following ranks as a preferential creditor?
Financial Advice Legal Concepts & Consid.w: Employees owed certain unpaid wages and holiday pay are treated as preferential creditors, ranking above unsecured creditors.

n.0: Shareholders rank last, not as preferential creditors.
n.2: Fixed charge lenders are secured, not preferential.
n.3: Trade suppliers are unsecured and rank lower.

Financial Advice Legal Concepts & Consid.q: Which event most commonly triggers the compulsory liquidation of a company?
o: The resignation of all of the directors
A failure to file the annual returns
Shareholders refusing to approve the accounts
A court order following a creditor's petition
Financial Advice Legal Concepts & Consid.w: Compulsory liquidation usually begins with a creditor's petition leading to a court order to wind up the company.

n.0: Directors resigning does not automatically cause it.
n.1: Late filing may prompt enforcement, not winding up.
n.2: Refusal of accounts requires rectification, not liquidation.

Financial Advice Legal Concepts & Consid.q: Which principle ensures that unsecured creditors are treated equally in an insolvency?
Financial Advice Legal Concepts & Consid.w: The pari passu principle requires unsecured creditors to share equally in available assets, in proportion to their claims.

n.0: The prescribed part reserves floating charge funds, not equal sharing.
n.1: Survivorship applies to co-owned property.
n.2: Privity concerns who can enforce contracts.

Financial Advice Legal Concepts & Consid.q: What is the typical automatic discharge period for a straightforward bankruptcy in England and Wales?
Financial Advice Legal Concepts & Consid.w: Most bankrupts are automatically discharged after 12 months, although restrictions may continue longer in serious cases.

n.0: 6 months is shorter than the statutory period.
n.2: 24 months is longer than the usual period.
n.3: 36 months relates to certain repayment plans, not discharge.

Financial Advice Legal Concepts & Consid.q: What is the role of a trustee?
o: To manage trust assets for the beneficiaries
To draft the original trust deed themselves
To inherit the property under intestacy rules
To provide probate services for the executors
Financial Advice Legal Concepts & Consid.w: Trustees hold and manage trust property under the trust deed for the benefit of beneficiaries, exercising fiduciary duties.

n.1: The settlor or solicitor drafts the deed, not the trustee.
n.2: Intestacy inheritance follows statute, not trusteeship.
n.3: Executors, not trustees, administer estates.

Financial Advice Legal Concepts & Consid.q: Which statement best describes the doctrine of agency by necessity?
o: An agent acquires authority through a regular established course of dealing
An agent acts without authority in an emergency to protect the principal
An agent may ratify their own acts without the principal's consent
An agent acts under statutory authority regardless of any consent
Financial Advice Legal Concepts & Consid.w: Agency by necessity lets an agent act without authority in an urgent situation to preserve the principal's property or interests.

n.0: Regular dealings create implied actual authority, not necessity.
n.2: Only the principal can ratify, not the agent.
n.3: Statutory authority is distinct from emergency necessity.

Financial Advice Legal Concepts & Consid.q: A testator leaves a letter of wishes alongside their will. What is the function of this document?
o: It overrides the express terms of the will
It imposes a binding trust obligation
It guides trustees but is not binding
It must be registered with the Probate Registry
Financial Advice Legal Concepts & Consid.w: A letter of wishes offers guidance to trustees or executors on the testator’s preferences, but it has no legal force.

n.0: It cannot override the formal terms of a will.
n.1: It imposes no binding legal obligation.
n.3: Registration is not required for it to take effect.

Financial Advice Legal Concepts & Consid.q: Two parties sign a contract to sell a painting that, unknown to both, had already been destroyed. Which doctrine applies to their shared, fundamental false assumption?
Financial Advice Legal Concepts & Consid.w: Common mistake may render a contract void where both parties are fundamentally mistaken about a fact central to the agreement.

n.0: Undue influence involves improper pressure, not shared error.
n.1: Estoppel concerns reliance on promises, not mutual mistake.
n.3: Misrepresentation involves one party's false statement.

Financial Advice Legal Concepts & Consid.q: Which situation demonstrates ratification in the law of agency?
o: An agent acts within the actual authority granted
A client signs a contract directly with the provider
A firm dismisses an agent for misconduct
A principal later approves an unauthorised act
Financial Advice Legal Concepts & Consid.w: Ratification occurs when a principal retrospectively approves an act done on their behalf without prior authority.

n.0: Acts within actual authority need no ratification.
n.1: A direct contract does not involve agency ratification.
n.2: Dismissing an agent is unrelated to ratification.

Financial Advice Legal Concepts & Consid.q: A client's Individual Voluntary Arrangement fails part-way through. What is the most likely outcome?
o: The debtor may face bankruptcy proceedings
The IVA is automatically extended for five years
The debtor is released from all remaining debts
The court annuls all of the creditors' claims
Financial Advice Legal Concepts & Consid.w: If an IVA fails, creditors may petition for the debtor's bankruptcy to recover debts through asset realisation.

n.1: An IVA does not extend automatically on failure.
n.2: Failure does not release the debtor; debts remain.
n.3: Creditors' claims remain valid, not annulled.

Financial Advice Legal Concepts & Consid.q: A trust’s beneficiaries are all adults and absolutely entitled. What does the rule in Saunders v Vautier allow them to do?
o: Extend the trust beyond the settlor’s instructions
Demand that the trust be terminated
Require intestacy rules to apply instead
Alter the terms of a will before probate
Financial Advice Legal Concepts & Consid.w: The rule lets all adult beneficiaries with absolute entitlement require the trustees to end the trust and distribute the assets.

n.0: Trustees cannot unilaterally extend a trust.
n.2: Beneficiaries cannot substitute intestacy for a valid will.
n.3: A will cannot be altered by beneficiaries before probate.

Financial Advice Legal Concepts & Consid.q: Which statement best describes the principle of privity of contract?
o: Third parties can always enforce beneficial contracts
Regulators can enforce any contract in their remit
Only parties to a contract can enforce it
Contracts must be written to be enforceable
Financial Advice Legal Concepts & Consid.w: Privity means only the parties to a contract have enforceable rights and obligations, subject to statutory exceptions.

n.0: Third parties enforce only where the 1999 Act applies.
n.1: Regulators enforce rules, not private contracts.
n.3: Contracts may be oral or implied.

Financial Advice Legal Concepts & Consid.q: A client on a low income has debts of £22,000 and almost no assets. Which procedure offers debt relief in this situation?
Financial Advice Legal Concepts & Consid.w: Debt Relief Orders are available to individuals with low income, debts under £30,000 and little or no assets, offering a cheaper alternative to bankruptcy.

n.0: IVAs suit larger debts and need creditor approval.
n.1: Bankruptcy is more costly and formal.
n.3: Compulsory liquidation applies to companies.

Financial Advice Legal Concepts & Consid.q: Which two statutory tests do the courts use to decide whether a company is insolvent?
Financial Advice Legal Concepts & Consid.w: The two statutory tests are the cash-flow test (inability to pay debts as they fall due) and the balance-sheet test (liabilities exceeding assets).

n.0: Liquidity preference is an economics concept.
n.1: Profitability ratios do not determine insolvency.
n.2: Capital adequacy applies to banks.

Financial Advice Legal Concepts & Consid.q: In a tenancy in common, what distinguishes ownership from a joint tenancy?
o: Ownership passes automatically to the surviving co-owner
Shares cannot be sold without all owners' consent
All parties must hold exactly equal shares
Each holds a distinct share passing by will
Financial Advice Legal Concepts & Consid.w: Tenancy in common gives each co-owner a distinct proportion that can be sold or left by will.

n.0: Survivorship is a feature of joint tenancy.
n.1: A co-owner may transfer their share subject to any trust.
n.2: Shares can be unequal; equality is not required.

Financial Advice Legal Concepts & Consid.q: Which best describes equitable ownership of property?
o: The right to benefit though another holds legal title
The right to enforce contracts in one's own name
The statutory title to land registered at HM Land Registry
The right to dispose of property regardless of legal title
Financial Advice Legal Concepts & Consid.w: Equitable ownership arises where one party enjoys the benefit of property while another holds legal title, as in trusts and nominee arrangements.

n.1: Contract enforcement concerns legal standing, not equitable ownership.
n.2: Registered legal title differs from an equitable interest.
n.3: Equitable owners cannot always dispose without the legal owner.

Financial Advice Legal Concepts & Consid.q: A will leaves a named diamond ring to a niece. What is this type of gift called?
Financial Advice Legal Concepts & Consid.w: A specific legacy is a gift of a particular identifiable item, such as a named ring or property.

n.0: A pecuniary legacy is a gift of money.
n.1: A residuary bequest is what remains after debts and legacies.
n.2: A demonstrative legacy is money paid from a named source.

Financial Advice Legal Concepts & Consid.q: What is the primary purpose of a winding-up petition?
o: To restructure the company's outstanding debts
To appoint directors in place of existing ones
To seek a court order to liquidate a company
To merge two insolvent companies together
Financial Advice Legal Concepts & Consid.w: A winding-up petition asks the court to liquidate a company that cannot pay its debts.

n.0: Restructuring results from administration or a CVA.
n.1: A petition begins liquidation, not director appointments.
n.3: Petitions dissolve companies, they do not merge them.

Financial Advice Legal Concepts & Consid.q: A client emails acceptance of adviser Tom's written offer at 18:00 on Friday and the firm's mailbox receives it instantly. When is acceptance generally effective for instantaneous communications?
o: When the adviser opens and reads it
When it reaches the firm's mailbox
Financial Advice Legal Concepts & Consid.w: For instantaneous communications like email, acceptance takes effect on receipt by the offeror's system, absent contrary terms.

n.0: Actual reading is not required; legal receipt suffices.
n.1: No default rule defers effect to business hours.
n.2: The postal rule (dispatch) does not apply to email.

Financial Advice Legal Concepts & Consid.q: Adviser Mark persuades an elderly, trusting client to sign an unsuitable investment agreement he would not otherwise have entered. Which contract law doctrine does this illustrate?
o: Common mistake as to the subject matter
Breach of an agent's apparent authority
Financial Advice Legal Concepts & Consid.w: Undue influence arises when one party exploits trust or pressure to secure a contract, which may render it voidable.

n.1: Mistake is a separate doctrine unrelated to improper pressure.
n.2: Authority issues concern agency, not exploitation of trust.
n.3: Frustration discharges contracts but is unconnected to undue influence.

Financial Advice Legal Concepts & Consid.q: Which debt is non-provable in bankruptcy, meaning creditors cannot claim it in the proceedings?
Financial Advice Legal Concepts & Consid.w: Criminal court fines are non-provable in bankruptcy and remain payable regardless of the proceedings.

n.0: Unsecured loans are provable debts.
n.1: Credit card balances are provable and usually discharged.
n.2: Utility arrears are provable unsecured liabilities.

Financial Advice Legal Concepts & Consid.q: Which of the following is an equitable remedy for breach of contract?
Financial Advice Legal Concepts & Consid.w: Specific performance is an equitable remedy compelling a party to perform obligations rather than pay damages.

n.0: Damages are a common law remedy.
n.2: Penalty clauses are generally unenforceable.
n.3: Liquidated damages are a contractual term, not equitable relief.

Financial Advice Legal Concepts & Consid.q: The insolvent company and a creditor owe each other money. Which principle allows those mutual debts to be offset?
Financial Advice Legal Concepts & Consid.w: Insolvency set-off requires mutual debts between the insolvent party and a creditor to be offset, leaving only the balance claimable.

n.0: Pari passu governs equal treatment, not set-off.
n.2: Privity governs who can enforce contracts.
n.3: Consideration concerns contract formation.

Financial Advice Legal Concepts & Consid.q: A client asks adviser Priya to explain a power of attorney before she appoints her son. Which statement best defines it?
o: A court order compelling third parties to act
A deed transferring full ownership to a representative
A document authorising another to act for the donor
A statutory right for advisers to manage client assets
Financial Advice Legal Concepts & Consid.w: A power of attorney is a legal instrument by which a donor appoints an attorney to act on their behalf in specified matters.

n.0: It is a private arrangement, not a court order.
n.1: It grants authority to act, not ownership of assets.
n.3: Advisers need regulatory authorisation, not this statutory right.

Financial Advice Legal Concepts & Consid.q: In a company insolvency, what is the role of a liquidator?
o: To restructure the company to avoid winding up
To supervise a debtor's repayments under an IVA
To advise the shareholders on future dividends
To realise assets and repay the creditors
Financial Advice Legal Concepts & Consid.w: The liquidator collects and realises the company's assets and distributes proceeds according to statutory priority before dissolution.

n.0: Restructuring is the function of administration.
n.1: IVAs apply to individuals, not companies.
n.2: Shareholders receive residual funds last, not advice from the liquidator.

Financial Advice Legal Concepts & Consid.q: A company wishes to reach a binding compromise with its creditors and avoid liquidation. Which statutory procedure allows this?
Financial Advice Legal Concepts & Consid.w: A CVA lets a company reach an agreement with its creditors, supervised by an insolvency practitioner, to repay debts over time while avoiding liquidation.

n.1: Administration may restructure but is not primarily a compromise.
n.2: Receivership enforces secured rights, not a compromise with all creditors.
n.3: Bankruptcy is an individual process.

Financial Advice Legal Concepts & Consid.q: Which trust gives a beneficiary a fixed right to the trust's income?
Financial Advice Legal Concepts & Consid.w: An interest in possession trust gives a beneficiary a fixed right to the trust income, unlike a discretionary trust.

n.0: Discretionary trusts give no fixed entitlement.
n.1: Protective trusts restrict access rather than guarantee income.
n.3: Constructive trusts are imposed by law.

Financial Advice Legal Concepts & Consid.q: Under the intestacy rules, how is a minor beneficiary’s inheritance dealt with until adulthood?
o: It is held on statutory trust until 18
It is transferred outright to their appointed guardians
The executors may distribute it at their own discretion
It is withheld until the beneficiary marries
Financial Advice Legal Concepts & Consid.w: Under intestacy, a minor’s entitlement is held on statutory trust until they reach 18.

n.1: Guardians care for minors but do not hold their inheritance.
n.2: Statutory trusts apply, so executors cannot distribute at will.
n.3: Marriage is not a condition of inheritance.

Financial Advice Legal Concepts & Consid.q: A director is disqualified under the Company Directors Disqualification Act 1986. What is the effect for the disqualification period?
o: They lose all of their personal assets automatically
They must personally repay all of the company's debts
They are barred from holding shares in any company
They cannot act as a director or in management
Financial Advice Legal Concepts & Consid.w: A disqualified director cannot act in management or directorship roles for the set period, but does not automatically lose assets or shares.

n.0: Personal assets are not automatically confiscated.
n.1: Directors are not automatically liable for all debts.
n.2: They may still own shares, just not manage companies.

Financial Advice Legal Concepts & Consid.q: Which element is NOT required to form a legally binding simple contract?
Financial Advice Legal Concepts & Consid.w: A simple contract needs offer, acceptance, consideration, intention and capacity; a deed is not required.

n.0: A clear offer and acceptance are required.
n.2: Intention to be bound is required.
n.3: Consideration is required unless made by deed.

Financial Advice Legal Concepts & Consid.q: An IVA has been approved for a client. Which role is appointed to oversee repayments to creditors?
Financial Advice Legal Concepts & Consid.w: An insolvency practitioner supervises the IVA, ensuring the debtor's repayments are distributed to creditors under the agreed terms.

n.1: The Official Receiver administers bankruptcies, not IVAs.
n.2: Directors cannot supervise IVAs.
n.3: Advisers may explain options but cannot supervise IVAs.

Financial Advice Legal Concepts & Consid.q: In a company liquidation, which creditor group is paid after preferential creditors but before unsecured creditors?
Financial Advice Legal Concepts & Consid.w: Floating charge holders are paid after preferential creditors, subject to the prescribed part reserved for unsecured creditors.

n.0: Fixed charge holders are paid first, before preferential creditors.
n.1: Trade creditors are unsecured and rank lower.
n.3: Shareholders are residual claimants, paid last.

Financial Advice Legal Concepts & Consid.q: A client married last month having made a will some years ago. What is the effect of the marriage on that will?
o: It automatically amends the will to include the new spouse
It revokes the will unless made in contemplation of it
It has no effect at all on the existing will
It revokes only the clauses relating to property
Financial Advice Legal Concepts & Consid.w: Under the Wills Act 1837, marriage revokes a will unless it was expressly made in contemplation of that marriage.

n.0: The law does not automatically amend wills.
n.2: Marriage does affect the will, subject to the exception.
n.3: The whole will is revoked, not only property clauses.

Financial Advice Legal Concepts & Consid.q: When a bank provides a mortgage loan, what interest does it usually hold in the property?
o: Full legal title to the property
Financial Advice Legal Concepts & Consid.w: The bank usually takes a legal charge over the property, securing repayment without owning it outright.

n.1: The borrower, not the bank, retains beneficial ownership.
n.2: Legal title passes only on repossession after default.
n.3: A tenancy in common is co-ownership, not security.

Financial Advice Legal Concepts & Consid.q: Which element of a valid contract ensures both parties intend their agreement to be legally enforceable?
Financial Advice Legal Concepts & Consid.w: For enforceability the parties must intend their agreement to create legal obligations.

n.0: Consideration is needed but is not intention.
n.1: An offer is needed but may be social in nature without intention.
n.2: Capacity enables contracting but does not prove intention.

Financial Advice Legal Concepts & Consid.q: Which situation would most likely give rise to a constructive trust?
o: Property held for another out of fairness
Two parties signing a deed of trust
A settlor transferring assets into a trust
Financial Advice Legal Concepts & Consid.w: Constructive trusts are imposed by courts to prevent unfairness, where it would be inequitable for one party to keep sole benefit.

n.1: A deed of trust creates an express trust.
n.2: A settlor creating a trust makes an express trust.
n.3: Executors distribute under a will, not a constructive trust.

Financial Advice Legal Concepts & Consid.q: A client holds shares through a bare trust and asks how the trustees may act. Which statement is correct?
o: Trustees actively manage the assets with full discretion
Trustees hold legal title, acting as beneficiaries direct
Trustees acquire beneficial ownership alongside legal title
The trust itself owns the assets as a legal entity
Financial Advice Legal Concepts & Consid.w: In a bare trust, trustees hold legal title but must act on the directions of beneficiaries, who hold the entire beneficial interest.

n.0: Full discretion describes a discretionary trust, not a bare trust.
n.2: Trustees hold legal title only, not beneficial ownership.
n.3: A trust is not itself a separate legal entity.

Financial Advice Legal Concepts & Consid.q: An agent contracts without authority, and the principal later refuses to accept the deal. Which principle explains why the principal is not bound?
Financial Advice Legal Concepts & Consid.w: If the principal refuses to ratify, the contract remains unauthorised and does not bind the principal.

n.0: Privity restricts enforcement to the parties, not ratification.
n.1: Consideration relates to enforceability, not ratification.
n.3: Survivorship is a property concept, not agency law.

Financial Advice Legal Concepts & Consid.q: An adviser recommends a trust giving a surviving spouse income for life while preserving capital for the children. Which trust is this?
Financial Advice Legal Concepts & Consid.w: A life interest trust gives the beneficiary, often a spouse, income for life while preserving the capital for others, such as children.

n.0: A discretionary trust gives trustees flexibility, not a fixed life interest.
n.2: A protective trust restricts access on bankruptcy.
n.3: A bare trust gives absolute entitlement.

Financial Advice Legal Concepts & Consid.q: A 16-year-old dies intestate in England and Wales. How is the estate treated?
o: It is automatically forfeited to the Crown
It passes to their parents or guardians
It is held in trust for their siblings
It is shared equally between friends and relatives
Financial Advice Legal Concepts & Consid.w: A minor cannot make a valid will, so on death the estate is distributed under intestacy, usually to the parents.

n.0: The Crown inherits only where no relatives survive.
n.2: Siblings do not inherit before parents.
n.3: Friends are not recognised under intestacy.

Financial Advice Legal Concepts & Consid.q: An executor needs authority to administer a deceased's estate under a valid will. Which document is required?
Financial Advice Legal Concepts & Consid.w: A grant of probate is issued by the court confirming the executor's authority to administer the estate.

n.0: A trust deed creates or governs trusts, not probate.
n.1: A codicil amends a will but is not probate authority.
n.2: A letter of wishes guides trustees but is not binding.

Financial Advice Legal Concepts & Consid.q: Which is an example of executed consideration in contract law?
o: A promise to pay in the future
Agreeing orally to pay a debt
Paying the premium at policy inception
Drafting a contract for later signature
Financial Advice Legal Concepts & Consid.w: Executed consideration is an act performed at the time of contracting, such as paying a premium immediately.

n.0: A future payment promise is executory, not executed.
n.1: An oral agreement without performance is not executed.
n.3: Drafting a contract provides no consideration yet.

Financial Advice Legal Concepts & Consid.q: A client holds an existing enduring power of attorney (EPA). Which statement most accurately describes it?
o: It is identical to an ordinary power of attorney
It remains valid after loss of capacity, if registered
It can only be used for health and welfare decisions
It becomes automatically invalid after the donor's death
Financial Advice Legal Concepts & Consid.w: EPAs, created before their replacement by LPAs, continue after incapacity provided they are registered with the OPG.

n.0: Ordinary powers end on incapacity; EPAs survive it.
n.2: EPAs cover property and financial affairs, not welfare.
n.3: Like all attorneys' powers, an EPA ends on death, not by rule of invalidity here.

Financial Advice Legal Concepts & Consid.q: A couple appoint a guardian in their wills. What is that guardian’s role?
o: To care for the couple’s minor children
To manage the trust property for the beneficiaries
To distribute the estate’s assets among its creditors
To draft later amendments to the wills
Financial Advice Legal Concepts & Consid.w: A guardian appointed in a will is responsible for the care of minor children if both parents die while the children are under 18.

n.1: Trustees, not guardians, manage trust property.
n.2: Executors distribute estate assets.
n.3: Guardians have no power to amend wills.

Financial Advice Legal Concepts & Consid.q: A settlor places assets in a discretionary trust for her grandchildren. How is ownership of those assets best described?
o: Beneficiaries hold both legal and beneficial ownership
The settlor retains legal ownership after creating the trust
Trustees acquire both legal and beneficial ownership
Trustees hold legal title; rights depend on discretion
Financial Advice Legal Concepts & Consid.w: Trustees hold legal title, while beneficiaries only have a right to be considered for distributions at the trustees' discretion.

n.0: Beneficiaries lack fixed beneficial ownership in a discretionary trust.
n.1: The settlor usually gives up ownership on creating the trust.
n.2: Trustees administer, not beneficially own, the assets.

Financial Advice Legal Concepts & Consid.q: Adviser Priya reviews four business structures for a client. Which is a separate legal person that can own property and contract in its own name?
o: A sole trader's registered business name
Financial Advice Legal Concepts & Consid.w: An LLP has separate legal personality: it can sue, be sued, own assets and contract independently of its members.

n.0: A general partnership has no separate personality; partners contract personally.
n.1: A sole trader and the business are the same legal person.
n.3: Unincorporated associations cannot generally hold property in their own name.

Financial Advice Legal Concepts & Consid.q: A discharged bankrupt asks which of his debts still remain payable. Which of the following is not written off by bankruptcy?
Financial Advice Legal Concepts & Consid.w: Certain debts, including student loans, court fines and child maintenance, survive bankruptcy and remain payable.

n.0: Credit card debts are generally discharged.
n.1: Unsecured personal loans are usually discharged.
n.2: Overdraft balances are unsecured and dischargeable.

Financial Advice Legal Concepts & Consid.q: A client wants to rescind an investment contract after a salesperson's false statement of fact induced them to enter it. Which doctrine primarily applies?
o: Common mistake making the contract void
Financial Advice Legal Concepts & Consid.w: An actionable misrepresentation, a false statement of fact inducing entry, makes the contract voidable, allowing rescission.

n.0: Common mistake voids a contract only in narrow shared-error cases.
n.1: Frustration concerns supervening events after formation.
n.3: Undue influence involves abuse of a trust relationship, not misstatement.

Financial Advice Legal Concepts & Consid.q: A company's directors keep trading although insolvency is unavoidable. Which statement correctly describes wrongful trading?
o: Directors may be personally liable for continuing to trade
Shareholders become liable once dividends are paid
Creditors are liable for accepting repayment from the company
Auditors are liable for failing to detect the insolvency
Financial Advice Legal Concepts & Consid.w: Wrongful trading occurs where directors knew, or ought to have known, there was no reasonable prospect of avoiding insolvency but continued trading, risking personal liability.

n.1: Shareholder liability is limited to unpaid share capital.
n.2: Creditors are not liable for accepting payments.
n.3: Auditors may face negligence claims, not wrongful trading.

Financial Advice Legal Concepts & Consid.q: Which insolvency process is designed to maximise creditor returns while giving a viable company a chance to survive?
Financial Advice Legal Concepts & Consid.w: Administration protects a company from enforcement while a strategy is pursued to rescue it or maximise creditor returns.

n.0: Liquidation focuses on dissolving the company.
n.2: Receivership benefits only the appointing creditor.
n.3: Bankruptcy applies to individuals.

Financial Advice Legal Concepts & Consid.q: Which party typically holds legal title in a unit trust structure?
Financial Advice Legal Concepts & Consid.w: In a unit trust the trustees hold legal title to the assets for unit holders, who have the beneficial interest.

n.0: Investors hold the beneficial, not legal, interest.
n.1: The manager directs investments but holds no title.
n.3: The FCA regulates funds; it holds no title.

Financial Advice Legal Concepts & Consid.q: Under the Trustee Act 2000, what must trustees do when investing trust funds?
o: Have regard to the standard investment criteria
Obtain beneficiaries’ consent for every decision
Financial Advice Legal Concepts & Consid.w: The Trustee Act 2000 requires trustees to have regard to the standard investment criteria, including suitability and diversification.

n.0: Trustees must act prudently but cannot guarantee returns.
n.1: They are not restricted to government bonds.
n.3: Routine investment decisions do not need beneficiary consent.

Financial Advice Legal Concepts & Consid.q: Which statement about mutual wills is correct?
o: They are identical wills made independently by spouses
They bind the parties not to revoke without consent
They automatically override the intestacy rules
They allow executors to alter provisions after death
Financial Advice Legal Concepts & Consid.w: Mutual wills rest on an agreement between two people not to revoke or alter their wills without the other’s consent, binding after the first death.

n.0: Identical independent wills are mirror wills.
n.2: Mutual wills bind contractually but do not override intestacy.
n.3: Executors cannot alter a valid will’s provisions.

Financial Advice Legal Concepts & Consid.q: In which situation could a director be accused of fraudulent trading?
o: Continuing trading while insolvent but without dishonest intent
Failing to file the annual accounts on time
Carrying on business with intent to defraud creditors
Paying secured creditors before unsecured creditors
Financial Advice Legal Concepts & Consid.w: Fraudulent trading involves deliberate intent to defraud creditors or a fraudulent purpose, and can lead to criminal liability.

n.0: Trading without intent to defraud may be wrongful trading.
n.1: Late filing breaches company law but is not fraud.
n.3: Paying secured creditors first is standard, not fraud.

Financial Advice Legal Concepts & Consid.q: A man dies intestate with no surviving spouse, children or parents. Who inherits his estate?
o: The executor of his last will
Financial Advice Legal Concepts & Consid.w: With no spouse, child or parent, the estate passes to siblings, then to wider relatives if none survive.

n.0: Friends are not recognised under intestacy.
n.1: Local authorities do not inherit estates.
n.2: Executors administer but do not inherit unless named.

Financial Advice Legal Concepts & Consid.q: An insolvent client wants protection from creditor enforcement while an IVA proposal is prepared. Which order provides this?
Financial Advice Legal Concepts & Consid.w: An interim order protects the debtor from creditor enforcement while an IVA proposal is being considered.

n.0: A charging order secures a debt against property.
n.2: An attachment of earnings deducts money from wages.
n.3: A possession order allows repossession, not protection.

Financial Advice Legal Concepts & Consid.q: A client dies leaving a spouse but no children. Under the current intestacy rules, how is the estate distributed?
o: The whole estate passes to the spouse
Half the estate passes to the siblings
It is divided between the spouse and parents
It passes automatically to the Crown
Financial Advice Legal Concepts & Consid.w: Since October 2014, where there are no children the surviving spouse or civil partner inherits the entire estate.

n.1: Siblings inherit only where there is no spouse.
n.2: Parents no longer share where a spouse survives with no children.
n.3: The Crown inherits only if no relatives survive.

Financial Advice Legal Concepts & Consid.q: An adviser describes a protective trust to a client. Which feature best defines this type of trust?
o: It restricts a beneficiary’s interest on their bankruptcy
It gives a beneficiary a fixed income for life
It confers immediate absolute entitlement on the beneficiary
It can be created only by an order of the court
Financial Advice Legal Concepts & Consid.w: A protective trust pays income to a beneficiary but converts into a discretionary trust if that beneficiary becomes bankrupt or tries to assign their interest.

n.1: Fixed lifetime income describes an interest in possession trust.
n.2: Immediate absolute entitlement describes a bare trust.
n.3: Protective trusts can be created by a settlor, not only by a court.

Financial Advice Legal Concepts & Consid.q: A platform's website displays fund prices to visitors. In contract terms, this is most likely to be what?
Financial Advice Legal Concepts & Consid.w: Price displays and lists are generally invitations to treat; the customer's order is the offer.

n.1: A binding offer would let mere ordering conclude a contract.
n.2: A counter-offer responds to an existing offer.
n.3: A unilateral offer invites performance, unlike a price display.

Financial Advice Legal Concepts & Consid.q: Which term describes a secured creditor with a claim over specific, identified company assets?
Financial Advice Legal Concepts & Consid.w: Fixed charge holders have security over specified assets, such as property or machinery, giving them first priority in liquidation.

n.1: Floating charges cover general assets and rank lower.
n.2: Preferential creditors include employees owed wages.
n.3: Contingent creditors are owed only if conditions occur.

Financial Advice Legal Concepts & Consid.q: During a company liquidation, which insolvency role investigates the conduct of the directors?
Financial Advice Legal Concepts & Consid.w: Liquidators must report on directors' conduct to the Insolvency Service, which may lead to disqualification proceedings.

n.0: The company secretary has administrative duties only.
n.1: A shareholders' committee has no investigatory powers.
n.3: The court registrar handles filings, not investigations.

Financial Advice Legal Concepts & Consid.q: A couple own their home as joint tenants. Which right attaches to a joint tenancy but not to a tenancy in common?
o: Ability to transfer a share by will
Individual power to sell a distinct share
Ownership held in separate beneficial shares
Financial Advice Legal Concepts & Consid.w: A joint tenancy carries the right of survivorship, so ownership passes automatically to the survivors on death.

n.1: Testamentary transfer belongs to tenancy in common.
n.2: Only tenants in common hold sellable distinct shares.
n.3: Separate beneficial shares define tenancy in common.

Financial Advice Legal Concepts & Consid.q: Under the Insolvency Act 1986, which of the following best describes bankruptcy?
o: A court order against an individual unable to pay debts
A voluntary arrangement agreed by a company's creditors
The compulsory winding up of a limited company
A debt management plan approved by the regulator
Financial Advice Legal Concepts & Consid.w: Bankruptcy is a court-based process for individuals unable to meet their debts, with assets realised to repay creditors.

n.1: A voluntary arrangement is separate and may prevent bankruptcy.
n.2: Compulsory winding up applies to companies, not individuals.
n.3: Debt management plans are informal, not court orders.

Financial Advice Legal Concepts & Consid.q: Under English law, which contract is unenforceable for lack of capacity?
Financial Advice Legal Concepts & Consid.w: Minors generally lack capacity for binding contracts, except for necessities or beneficial contracts of service.

n.1: An adult generally has full capacity to contract.
n.2: A company is a legal person able to contract.
n.3: A partnership can contract in its business name.

Financial Advice Legal Concepts & Consid.q: Which insolvency process applies specifically to a company incorporated under the Companies Act?
Financial Advice Legal Concepts & Consid.w: Liquidation is the process of winding up a company, realising its assets for creditors under the Companies Act and Insolvency Act.

n.0: Bankruptcy applies to individuals, not companies.
n.1: Debt Relief Orders are individual remedies.
n.3: IVAs are designed for individuals.

Financial Advice Legal Concepts & Consid.q: Which factor distinguishes actual authority from apparent authority in agency law?
o: Actual authority arises only in emergencies; apparent is always implied
Apparent authority must be written; actual authority is always oral
Actual authority always requires later ratification; apparent never does
Actual authority is granted by the principal; apparent arises from reliance
Financial Advice Legal Concepts & Consid.w: Actual authority comes from the principal's express or implied grant; apparent authority arises when a third party reasonably relies on a representation of authority.

n.0: Emergencies relate to agency by necessity, not actual authority.
n.1: Authority can be written or oral; this is wrong.
n.2: Actual authority is valid when granted, needing no ratification.

Financial Advice Legal Concepts & Consid.q: Which debt is excluded from discharge in bankruptcy on public policy grounds?
Financial Advice Legal Concepts & Consid.w: Debts obtained by fraud or dishonesty are excluded from discharge, so that misconduct is not rewarded by bankruptcy protection.

n.0: Bank loans are dischargeable in bankruptcy.
n.1: Credit card debts are normally discharged.
n.3: Utility arrears are unsecured and dischargeable.

Financial Advice Legal Concepts & Consid.q: Which requirement must be met before an attorney can use a Property and Financial Affairs LPA?
o: It must be witnessed by a solicitor and doctor
It only takes effect after capacity is lost
It must be registered with the OPG
It must be lodged at the Court of Protection first
Financial Advice Legal Concepts & Consid.w: An LPA must be registered with the OPG before use; a Property and Financial Affairs LPA can, if the donor wishes, be used while they still have capacity.

n.0: A certificate provider and witnesses suffice; a doctor is not required.
n.1: This LPA can be used before capacity is lost unless restricted.
n.3: Lodging at the Court of Protection is not routinely needed.

Financial Advice Legal Concepts & Consid.q: A person dies intestate with no surviving relatives. What happens to their estate?
o: It is retained by the probate registry
It is shared among local charities
It is transferred to the Insolvency Service
Financial Advice Legal Concepts & Consid.w: If no entitled relatives survive, the estate passes to the Crown as bona vacantia.

n.0: The probate registry does not retain estates.
n.1: Charities benefit only if named in a will.
n.2: The Insolvency Service does not handle intestate estates.

Financial Advice Legal Concepts & Consid.q: Which statement best explains why a company is considered a legal person?
o: It is owned collectively by its shareholders
It has separate personality from its members
It is managed by directors for shareholders
It can only contract through its employees
Financial Advice Legal Concepts & Consid.w: A company has separate legal personality under the Companies Act, letting it contract, sue and own property in its own name.

n.0: Shareholders own shares, not the company's assets.
n.2: Management by directors is a consequence, not the definition.
n.3: Companies can contract through various agents.

Financial Advice Legal Concepts & Consid.q: A client wishes to unwind a contract induced by misrepresentation and be returned to their pre-contractual position. Which remedy achieves this?
Financial Advice Legal Concepts & Consid.w: Rescission unwinds a contract, attempting to return both parties to the position they held before it was made.

n.0: Specific performance compels performance, not reversal.
n.1: Damages compensate loss, not restore the prior position.
n.2: Rectification corrects written errors only.

Financial Advice Legal Concepts & Consid.q: An adviser refers a client to their trust deed. Which of the following correctly describes this document?
o: A probate document granting executors their authority
A statutory form used to apply intestacy rules
A codicil that amends an existing will
The legal document setting out a trust’s terms
Financial Advice Legal Concepts & Consid.w: A trust deed is the legal instrument that creates a trust and governs trustee powers and beneficiary rights.

n.0: A grant of probate, not a trust deed, gives executors authority.
n.1: Intestacy is governed by statute, not by a deed.
n.2: A codicil amends a will, not a trust.

Financial Advice Legal Concepts & Consid.q: Which bodies authorise and regulate insolvency practitioners in the UK?
Financial Advice Legal Concepts & Consid.w: Insolvency practitioners are authorised and regulated by Recognised Professional Bodies, such as ICAEW and IPA, overseen by the Insolvency Service.

n.1: The FCA regulates financial services, not practitioners.
n.2: The PRA supervises banks and insurers.
n.3: The CMA focuses on competition and consumer law.

Financial Advice Legal Concepts & Consid.q: A will requires a beneficiary to outlive the testator by 28 days or the gift fails. Which rule is this?
Financial Advice Legal Concepts & Consid.w: A survivorship clause requires a beneficiary to survive the testator by a set period, commonly 28 days, or the gift lapses.

n.1: Intestacy applies only where there is no valid gift.
n.2: Per stirpes governs distribution among descendants.
n.3: Anti-lapse provisions apply to certain relatives, not survival periods.

Financial Advice Legal Concepts & Consid.q: A settlor wants trustees to decide how and when her beneficiaries receive benefits. Which trust best achieves this?
o: A trust giving each beneficiary a fixed income
A trust that must distribute all income equally
A trust where the settlor keeps full control
Financial Advice Legal Concepts & Consid.w: In a discretionary trust, the trustees decide how and when beneficiaries receive benefits, giving flexibility in estate planning.

n.0: Fixed entitlements describe a fixed-interest trust.
n.1: Discretionary trusts allow selective distribution, not mandatory equal shares.
n.3: The settlor gives up control to the trustees.

Financial Advice Legal Concepts & Consid.q: What is the main purpose of administration as a corporate insolvency procedure?
o: To protect the company from creditor action while restructuring
To repay shareholders ahead of creditors
Financial Advice Legal Concepts & Consid.w: Administration provides breathing space from creditor enforcement to attempt a rescue or restructuring of the company.

n.0: Dissolution is the outcome of liquidation.
n.2: Creditors, not shareholders, are prioritised.
n.3: Directors may be displaced, but not always permanently.

Financial Advice Legal Concepts & Consid.q: What is the effect of the Inheritance (Provision for Family and Dependants) Act 1975?
o: It lets dependants claim reasonable provision
It revokes a person's will automatically on divorce
It prevents any gifts being made to foreign beneficiaries
It ensures that children always inherit in equal shares
Financial Advice Legal Concepts & Consid.w: The Act allows dependants to claim reasonable financial provision where a will or intestacy does not provide adequately for them.

n.1: Divorce affects wills separately; this Act concerns provision.
n.2: The Act does not prohibit overseas gifts.
n.3: Children do not always inherit equally.

Financial Advice Legal Concepts & Consid.q: Before insolvency, a debtor transfers assets cheaply to put them beyond creditors' reach. Which mechanism lets creditors challenge this?
Financial Advice Legal Concepts & Consid.w: Transactions at undervalue can be challenged where a debtor disposed of assets for less than fair value before insolvency, prejudicing creditors.

n.0: Floating charge rules govern security ranking, not disposals.
n.1: Frustration deals with contract discharge.
n.2: Set-off offsets mutual debts, not asset transfers.

Financial Advice Legal Concepts & Consid.q: Which statement about mirror wills is correct?
o: They are joint wills that cannot be changed after a death
They automatically transfer all property to the children
They are two similar wills, usually made by spouses
They are informal oral wills recognised in emergencies
Financial Advice Legal Concepts & Consid.w: Mirror wills are two separate wills with similar terms, commonly used by spouses leaving estates to each other or the same beneficiaries.

n.0: Joint wills bind after the first death; mirror wills can change.
n.1: They do not transfer to children unless expressly stated.
n.3: Oral wills are valid only in limited military or maritime cases.

Financial Advice Legal Concepts & Consid.q: Under agency principles, an appointed representative's acts in regulated business are treated in law as whose acts?
Financial Advice Legal Concepts & Consid.w: An AR acts as agent of its authorised principal, which is responsible to clients for regulated activities within the appointment.

n.0: Liability attaches to the principal, not the AR alone.
n.1: A product provider is not the principal here.
n.2: Compliance officers supervise but are not the principal.

Financial Advice Legal Concepts & Consid.q: A platform's nominee company holds client investments. Who typically holds legal title and who holds beneficial title?
o: Clients hold legal; nominee holds beneficial
Nominee holds legal; clients hold beneficial
Provider holds both legal and beneficial
The FCA holds legal; clients hold beneficial
Financial Advice Legal Concepts & Consid.w: In custody arrangements the nominee holds legal title while end-investors keep the beneficial interest.

n.0: Clients do not hold legal title in a nominee structure.
n.2: Segregation prevents the provider holding clients' beneficial interest.
n.3: The FCA regulates; it holds no client title.

Financial Advice Legal Concepts & Consid.q: Under intestacy, how is an estate divided where a deceased child’s own children take that child’s share?
Financial Advice Legal Concepts & Consid.w: Per stirpes distribution means the children of a deceased heir inherit their parent’s share, preserving family branches.

n.0: Per capita gives equal shares to living heirs.
n.1: Pari passu applies in insolvency.
n.2: Survivorship applies to jointly held property.

Financial Advice Legal Concepts & Consid.q: Which requirement must be met for a will to be a valid holographic will?
o: It must be typed and witnessed by two solicitors
It must be sealed and formally notarised
It must be handwritten and signed by the testator
It must be registered with the Probate Registry
Financial Advice Legal Concepts & Consid.w: A holographic will is written entirely by hand and signed by the testator, subject to local recognition rules.

n.0: Typed wills can be valid but are not holographic.
n.1: Sealing and notarisation are not standard requirements.
n.3: Registration is not needed for validity in England and Wales.

Financial Advice Legal Concepts & Consid.q: Which of the following best describes a charitable trust?
o: It must serve legally recognised charitable purposes
It must share income equally among family members
It requires the express approval of the Crown
Financial Advice Legal Concepts & Consid.w: A charitable trust must have purposes recognised in law as charitable, such as relief of poverty or advancement of education, and benefit the public.

n.1: Charitable trusts serve the public, not family members.
n.2: They can last indefinitely, not just 21 years.
n.3: They register with the Charity Commission, not gain Crown approval.

Financial Advice Legal Concepts & Consid.q: Which feature of a company limited by shares protects its shareholders?
o: Full legal title to company assets
Financial Advice Legal Concepts & Consid.w: Shareholders' liability is limited to any unpaid amount on their shares, protecting personal assets from company debts.

n.1: Dividends depend on profits and board decisions.
n.2: Company assets belong to the company, not shareholders.
n.3: Shareholders may still lose their investment on insolvency.

Financial Advice Legal Concepts & Consid.q: Shares are held in the name of a nominee company for an investor's benefit. Which describes the ownership?
o: Nominee holds both legal and beneficial
Beneficial with nominee, legal with investor
Nominee holds legal; investor holds beneficial
Both legal and beneficial with the custodian
Financial Advice Legal Concepts & Consid.w: In nominee arrangements the nominee holds legal title as a bare trustee, while the investor keeps the beneficial interest.

n.0: A nominee does not take the beneficial interest.
n.1: The investor gives up legal title to the nominee.
n.3: A custodian holds legal, not beneficial, title.

Financial Advice Legal Concepts & Consid.q: What is the purpose of the 'prescribed part' in insolvency law?
o: To guarantee payment in full to fixed charge holders
To reserve floating funds for unsecured creditors
To reimburse directors' salaries before insolvency
To compensate the shareholders during liquidation
Financial Advice Legal Concepts & Consid.w: The prescribed part ring-fences a portion of floating charge realisations for unsecured creditors, improving fairness in distributions.

n.0: Fixed charge holders are paid first; the prescribed part does not apply.
n.2: Directors' salaries are not prioritised by it.
n.3: Shareholders rank last and do not benefit from it.

Financial Advice Legal Concepts & Consid.q: For what maximum period can a bankruptcy restrictions order extend restrictions on a bankrupt guilty of misconduct?
Financial Advice Legal Concepts & Consid.w: A bankruptcy restrictions order can extend restrictions for up to 15 years in cases of misconduct.

n.1: 3 years is far below the statutory maximum.
n.2: 7 years is within range but not the maximum.
n.3: 10 years may be imposed but is not the limit.

Financial Advice Legal Concepts & Consid.q: Which type of trust gives trustees full discretion over when and how beneficiaries benefit?
Financial Advice Legal Concepts & Consid.w: A discretionary trust lets trustees decide how and when beneficiaries benefit, offering flexibility in estate planning.

n.0: A bare trust confers fixed, absolute entitlement.
n.2: An interest in possession trust gives a fixed right to income.
n.3: A charitable trust must serve recognised charitable purposes.

Financial Advice Legal Concepts & Consid.q: A struggling company enters administration. What is the administrator's primary role?
o: To liquidate the assets and dissolve the company
To represent shareholders in the insolvency proceedings
To rescue the company as a going concern where possible
To supervise the directors in their daily activities
Financial Advice Legal Concepts & Consid.w: An administrator's primary aim is to rescue the company as a going concern, or otherwise achieve a better outcome for creditors than liquidation.

n.0: Liquidation is a separate process run by a liquidator.
n.1: Administrators act for creditors, not shareholders.
n.3: Administrators take over management, not supervise routine duties.

Financial Advice Legal Concepts & Consid.q: Why do trustees owe fiduciary duties to the beneficiaries of a trust?
o: Because they are personally entitled to the trust property
Because they inherit the property under intestacy
Because they must act in the beneficiaries’ best interests
Because they guarantee financial returns to the beneficiaries
Financial Advice Legal Concepts & Consid.w: Trustees are fiduciaries who must act in good faith, avoid conflicts of interest, and serve solely the beneficiaries’ best interests.

n.0: Trustees hold legal title but no beneficial entitlement.
n.1: Intestacy distributes property by statute, not through trusteeship.
n.3: Trustees must act prudently but cannot guarantee returns.

Financial Advice Legal Concepts & Consid.q: A client wants to know the formalities for a valid will. Which of the following is a requirement under English law?
o: It must be handwritten throughout by the testator
It must be registered with the Probate Registry
It must be written, signed and witnessed by two
It must be notarised by a practising solicitor
Financial Advice Legal Concepts & Consid.w: Under the Wills Act 1837 a valid will must be in writing, signed by the testator, and witnessed by two independent witnesses.

n.0: A will may be typed; handwriting is not required.
n.1: Registration is not mandatory for validity.
n.3: Notarisation is not required, only witnessing.

Financial Advice Legal Concepts & Consid.q: A client dies leaving no spouse, children, parents or siblings. Under the intestacy rules, who inherits the estate?
o: More distant relatives such as uncles and aunts
The local authority where they lived
Financial Advice Legal Concepts & Consid.w: Intestacy rules pass the estate to increasingly distant relatives, such as uncles, aunts or cousins, before it goes to the Crown.
