n.0: Friends are not recognised heirs under intestacy.
n.2: Local authorities do not inherit under intestacy.
n.3: Administrators manage the estate but do not inherit unless also entitled relatives.

Financial Advice Legal Concepts & Consid.q: Which scenario most clearly gives an adviser apparent (ostensible) authority to act for a firm?
o: The firm represents the adviser as authorised and the client relies
The adviser privately believes they have authority though never appointed
The client assumes authority because the adviser sounds confident
The adviser exceeds written limits but hides this from the client
Financial Advice Legal Concepts & Consid.w: Apparent authority arises where the principal represents that the agent has authority and a third party reasonably relies on it.

n.1: An agent's own belief does not bind the principal.
n.2: A client's assumption without a representation is insufficient.
n.3: Hidden limits alone do not create apparent authority.

Financial Advice Legal Concepts & Consid.q: Which of the following best defines a pecuniary legacy in a will?
o: A gift of land or property
A share of the residue of the estate
Financial Advice Legal Concepts & Consid.w: A pecuniary legacy is a fixed gift of money, such as £10,000 to a named person.

n.0: Personal possessions given specifically are specific legacies.
n.2: Gifts of land are specific devises.
n.3: A share of what remains is a residuary legacy.

Financial Advice Legal Concepts & Consid.q: Which term describes a liquidator continuing to trade to maximise creditor returns after liquidation has begun?
Financial Advice Legal Concepts & Consid.w: Liquidators may permit trading in liquidation where it benefits creditors by maximising the realisation of assets.

n.0: Fraudulent trading involves intent to defraud creditors.
n.1: Wrongful trading concerns directors, not liquidators.
n.3: Receivership is enforcement by secured creditors.

Financial Advice Legal Concepts & Consid.q: Which insolvency officer is appointed to manage an individual's estate during bankruptcy?
Financial Advice Legal Concepts & Consid.w: The trustee in bankruptcy takes control of the bankrupt's assets, realises them and distributes the funds to creditors.

n.1: Liquidators deal with companies, not individuals.
n.2: Company secretaries manage corporate administration.
n.3: Court registrars handle filings, not estates.

Financial Advice Legal Concepts & Consid.q: Which principle is engaged if a client contract is formed for an illegal purpose?
o: Undue influence lets a court set it aside
Illegality makes it void ab initio
Financial Advice Legal Concepts & Consid.w: A contract formed for an illegal purpose is void ab initio, so it never had legal effect.

n.0: Misrepresentation makes a contract voidable, not void.
n.1: Frustration arises from supervening events, not illegality.
n.2: Undue influence concerns improper pressure, not illegality.

Financial Advice Legal Concepts & Consid.q: A residuary beneficiary named in a will dies before the testator. What generally happens to that gift?
o: It passes automatically to the executor
It usually lapses unless a substitute is named
It is redirected to the Crown
It is divided equally between all remaining relatives
Financial Advice Legal Concepts & Consid.w: If a residuary beneficiary predeceases the testator, the gift usually lapses unless the will names a substitute or anti-lapse rules apply.

n.0: Executors do not inherit unless also named.
n.2: The Crown inherits only where no heirs exist.
n.3: Division follows the will or intestacy, not arbitrary shares.

Financial Advice Legal Concepts & Consid.q: Which UK body administers bankruptcy and company liquidation cases?
Financial Advice Legal Concepts & Consid.w: The Insolvency Service administers bankruptcies and company liquidations through the Official Receiver and supports the regulation of practitioners.

n.1: The Bank of England handles monetary policy and stability.
n.2: The SFO prosecutes fraud, not insolvencies.
n.3: The FOS resolves disputes, not insolvency administration.

Financial Advice Legal Concepts & Consid.q: Which of the following is an example of a demonstrative legacy?
o: A gold ring left to a niece
Half the residue left to a spouse
A house gifted to a child
£5,000 paid from a named bank account
Financial Advice Legal Concepts & Consid.w: A demonstrative legacy is a gift of money payable from a specified source, such as a named account or fund.

n.0: A gift of a ring is a specific legacy.
n.1: A share of the residue is a residuary legacy.
n.2: A gift of a house is a specific devise.

Financial Advice Legal Concepts & Consid.q: Which rule causes a gift to fail where the beneficiary dies before the testator?
o: The rule in Saunders v Vautier
Financial Advice Legal Concepts & Consid.w: Under the doctrine of lapse a gift fails if the beneficiary dies before the testator, unless a substitution or statutory saving applies.

n.0: The rule against perpetuities limits trust duration.
n.1: Saunders v Vautier allows beneficiaries to end a trust.
n.3: The forfeiture rule bars unlawful killers from inheriting.

Financial Advice Legal Concepts & Consid.q: A secured lender wants to recover money from assets subject to a floating charge. Which procedure is commonly used?
Financial Advice Legal Concepts & Consid.w: Administrative receivership allows a floating charge holder to appoint a receiver to realise company assets and repay the debt.

n.0: Compulsory liquidation is not initiated by secured lenders.
n.2: Debt Relief Orders apply only to individuals.
n.3: IVAs are arrangements for individuals.

Financial Advice Legal Concepts & Consid.q: A client wants to make a small change to his existing will without rewriting it. Which of the following is true of a codicil?
o: It amends an existing will without replacing it
It automatically revokes the original will
It is valid only if handwritten by the testator
It is valid only once registered at the Probate Registry
Financial Advice Legal Concepts & Consid.w: A codicil amends or adds to a will without replacing it, and must meet the same formal requirements as a will.

n.1: A codicil supplements a will, it does not revoke it.
n.2: Codicils may be typed, not only handwritten.
n.3: Registration is not required for validity.

Financial Advice Legal Concepts & Consid.q: What is the maximum perpetuity period for a private trust under the Perpetuities and Accumulations Act 2009?
Financial Advice Legal Concepts & Consid.w: The Perpetuities and Accumulations Act 2009 sets a single statutory perpetuity period of 125 years for private trusts.

n.1: 80 years applied under the earlier regime but has been superseded.
n.2: 100 years is not the statutory figure.
n.3: 150 years exceeds the statutory maximum.

Financial Advice Legal Concepts & Consid.q: In a company liquidation, which category of creditor is paid first?
Financial Advice Legal Concepts & Consid.w: Fixed charge holders rank first because their security attaches to specific assets and is enforceable outside the liquidation estate.

n.0: Unsecured creditors rank below secured and preferential creditors.
n.2: Floating charge holders rank after preferential creditors.
n.3: Trade creditors are unsecured and rank lower.

Financial Advice Legal Concepts & Consid.q: Which insolvency process lets a secured creditor appoint a receiver to realise assets subject to a fixed or floating charge?
Financial Advice Legal Concepts & Consid.w: Receivership enables a secured creditor to appoint a receiver to realise charged assets and repay the debt owed to them.

n.0: Liquidation is not initiated directly by secured creditors.
n.1: A CVA is a compromise, not enforcement of security.
n.3: Administration aims to rescue the business, not enforce security.

Financial Advice Legal Concepts & Consid.q: Which of these assets usually passes outside a will or the intestacy rules?
o: Shares held in a private company
Jointly owned property passing by survivorship
Cash held in a sole-name bank account
Financial Advice Legal Concepts & Consid.w: Property held as joint tenants passes automatically to the survivor, outside the will or intestacy process.

n.0: Solely owned jewellery passes under the will or intestacy.
n.1: Private company shares form part of the estate unless joint.
n.3: Sole bank accounts are estate assets.

Financial Advice Legal Concepts & Consid.q: A creditor asks what minimum debt is required to petition for an individual's bankruptcy in England and Wales. What is the figure?
Financial Advice Legal Concepts & Consid.w: Since 2015, the threshold for a creditor's bankruptcy petition in England and Wales has been £5,000.

n.0: £750 was the threshold used before April 2015.
n.2: £10,000 is above the statutory minimum.
n.3: £15,000 exceeds the required figure.

Financial Advice Legal Concepts & Consid.q: A client wants to repay debts over time under a formal arrangement and avoid bankruptcy. Which procedure suits this?
Financial Advice Legal Concepts & Consid.w: An IVA is a formal agreement approved by creditors that allows debts to be repaid over time and avoids bankruptcy.

n.0: Debt Relief Orders suit low-debt cases with minimal assets.
n.1: Compulsory liquidation applies to companies.
n.2: Administration orders apply to companies, not individuals.

Financial Advice Legal Concepts & Consid.q: A client posts a signed acceptance of an insurer's offer, but the letter is delayed in the post. Under the postal rule, when does acceptance take effect?
o: Only once consideration has been provided
When the acceptance is properly posted
When the offeror actually reads the letter
When received by the offeror at their address
Financial Advice Legal Concepts & Consid.w: The postal rule provides that acceptance is effective when properly posted, even if it is delayed or lost, unless excluded.

n.0: Consideration is a separate requirement, not the trigger for acceptance.
n.2: Reading by the offeror is not required under the postal rule.
n.3: Receipt governs instantaneous communications, not posted acceptances.

Financial Advice Legal Concepts & Consid.q: Which principle lets a court imply a term into a contract to give it business efficacy?
Financial Advice Legal Concepts & Consid.w: The officious bystander test implies a term so obvious both parties would have agreed to it if asked.

n.0: Consideration concerns the bargain, not implied terms.
n.2: Frustration deals with impossibility, not implication.
n.3: The postal rule concerns timing of acceptance.

Financial Advice Legal Concepts & Consid.q: A sole trader can no longer pay his business debts. Which insolvency process applies to him, as it would to any individual?
Financial Advice Legal Concepts & Consid.w: Sole traders are individuals, so bankruptcy is the equivalent process, allowing debts to be written off and assets realised.

n.0: CVAs apply to companies, not sole traders.
n.1: Administration is a corporate process.
n.3: Liquidation applies to companies.

The Regulation of Financial Services.q: Which EU regulation improved transparency in derivatives markets?
The Regulation of Financial Services.w: The European Market Infrastructure Regulation (EMIR) introduced central clearing, reporting and risk mitigation for OTC derivatives.

n.0: MiFID II governs securities markets, not derivatives clearing.
n.2: UCITS covers investment funds, not derivatives.
n.3: PSD2 regulates payments, not derivatives.

The Regulation of Financial Services.q: Which UK body enforces criminal law against serious market fraud?
The Regulation of Financial Services.w: The Serious Fraud Office investigates and prosecutes serious or complex fraud, including some market-related fraud.

n.0: The FCA enforces civil and regulatory sanctions, not serious criminal fraud.
n.1: The PRA focuses on prudential regulation.
n.2: The FRC oversees reporting and audit standards.

The Regulation of Financial Services.q: At the global level, which body coordinates prudential supervision standards for internationally active banks?
The Regulation of Financial Services.w: The Basel Committee on Banking Supervision develops global standards on bank capital adequacy, stress testing and liquidity.

n.0: The International Organization of Securities Commissions sets securities standards, not bank prudential rules.
n.1: The Financial Action Task Force leads AML, not bank capital.
n.2: The International Monetary Fund monitors stability but sets no bank standards.

The Regulation of Financial Services.q: Which professional body awards chartered status to financial planners in the UK?
The Regulation of Financial Services.w: The Chartered Insurance Institute awards chartered status and sets professional standards for financial planners and advisers.

n.0: The Institute and Faculty of Actuaries regulates actuaries, not financial planners.
n.1: The Financial Conduct Authority regulates conduct but awards no chartered status.
n.3: The Competition and Markets Authority enforces competition, not qualifications.

The Regulation of Financial Services.q: Which regulator approves prospectuses for securities listings in the UK?
The Regulation of Financial Services.w: The FCA approves prospectuses for securities listings, ensuring investor disclosure and market integrity.

n.0: The PRA supervises prudential risk.
n.1: The Bank does not oversee prospectus approval.
n.2: The CMA handles competition law.

The Regulation of Financial Services.q: Which body acts as the UK resolution authority for failing banks?
The Regulation of Financial Services.w: The Bank of England is the UK resolution authority responsible for executing resolution tools.

n.0: The FCA focuses on conduct, not resolution.
n.1: The PRA supervises prudential risks.
n.3: The FSCS compensates eligible claimants.

The Regulation of Financial Services.q: Which body oversees anti-money laundering supervision for solicitors in England and Wales?
The Regulation of Financial Services.w: The Solicitors Regulation Authority supervises anti-money laundering compliance for law firms under the Money Laundering Regulations.

n.0: The FCA supervises financial firms, not solicitors.
n.2: The PRA oversees prudential soundness of banks and insurers.
n.3: The CMA oversees competition policy.

The Regulation of Financial Services.q: Which statutory body provides oversight of the trustees who run occupational pension schemes in the UK?
The Regulation of Financial Services.w: The Pensions Regulator oversees pension scheme trustees to ensure schemes are properly funded and governed.

n.0: The Financial Conduct Authority supervises personal pensions and conduct, not scheme trustees.
n.1: The Competition and Markets Authority enforces competition, not pensions.
n.3: The Serious Fraud Office investigates fraud, not pension governance.

The Regulation of Financial Services.q: What is the PRA’s approach to authorisation under FSMA?
o: Ensuring the best product pricing for customers
Requiring conduct fines before any approval
The Regulation of Financial Services.w: In authorising firms the PRA assesses whether they meet prudential threshold conditions to ensure soundness and resilience.

n.0: Product pricing is an FCA conduct issue.
n.1: Fines are enforcement outcomes, not part of authorisation.
n.2: Prospectus approval is the FCA’s responsibility.

The Regulation of Financial Services.q: For a new bank application under Part 4A FSMA, which combination is required?
o: FCA authorisation with the PRA’s consent
HM Treasury approval followed by an FCA licence
PRA authorisation with the FCA’s consent
Bank of England Court approval then PRA consent
The Regulation of Financial Services.w: Banks are authorised by the PRA for prudential purposes, but the PRA must obtain the FCA’s consent on conduct before granting Part 4A permission.

n.0: For banks the FCA is not the lead decision-maker.
n.1: Treasury sets the framework but does not approve licences.
n.3: The Court oversees governance, not authorisations.

The Regulation of Financial Services.q: Which Bank of England committee decides the level of the UK’s official Bank Rate?
The Regulation of Financial Services.w: The MPC sets the official Bank Rate to meet the government’s inflation target and maintain monetary stability.

n.0: The FPC sets macroprudential tools.
n.2: The PRC oversees prudential regulation.
n.3: The Court manages governance.

The Regulation of Financial Services.q: At the international level, which body issues principles for effective securities regulation across markets?
The Regulation of Financial Services.w: IOSCO develops international principles for securities regulators to promote fair, efficient and resilient markets.

n.0: The Basel Committee on Banking Supervision focuses on banks, not securities.
n.1: The Financial Stability Board coordinates broadly but IOSCO sets securities principles.
n.2: The International Monetary Fund monitors stability, not securities regulation.

The Regulation of Financial Services.q: Which UK statutory framework requires banks to prepare 'living wills' for orderly wind-down if needed?
The Regulation of Financial Services.w: The Banking Act 2009 introduced recovery and resolution planning, requiring banks to prepare 'living wills' for orderly wind-down.

n.0: The MiFID II Directive governs markets and investor protection, not wind-down.
n.2: The Solvency II Directive applies to insurers, not banks.
n.3: The UCITS Directive covers investment funds, not bank recovery.

The Regulation of Financial Services.q: Which organisation is responsible for monitoring compliance with the UK Corporate Governance Code by listed companies?
The Regulation of Financial Services.w: The Financial Reporting Council monitors compliance with the UK Corporate Governance Code to improve accountability in listed companies.

n.0: The Financial Conduct Authority enforces listing rules but does not oversee the Code.
n.1: The Competition and Markets Authority handles competition issues, not governance codes.
n.3: The Prudential Regulation Authority oversees prudential risk, not governance codes.

The Regulation of Financial Services.q: Within the UK, which organisation is responsible for investigating breaches of the UK Corporate Governance Code?
The Regulation of Financial Services.w: The Financial Reporting Council investigates compliance with the UK Corporate Governance Code and accountability of listed firms.

n.0: The Financial Conduct Authority enforces market conduct, not governance codes.
n.1: The Prudential Regulation Authority oversees prudential risk, not governance codes.
n.2: The Bank of England manages stability, not governance compliance.

The Regulation of Financial Services.q: Where is the FCA’s primary accountability to Parliament exercised?
o: Via the Bank of England’s Court
The Regulation of Financial Services.w: The FCA is accountable to Parliament primarily through the scrutiny of the Treasury Select Committee.

n.1: The MPC handles monetary policy.
n.2: The Competition Appeal Tribunal hears competition cases.
n.3: The Court oversees Bank governance.

The Regulation of Financial Services.q: Which body regulates and authorises UK actuaries?
o: The Institute and Faculty of Actuaries
The Regulation of Financial Services.w: The Institute and Faculty of Actuaries regulates its members, setting professional standards and authorising actuaries.

n.1: The FRC sets standards but does not individually authorise actuaries.
n.2: The FCA does not regulate the actuarial profession.
n.3: The PRA supervises insurers that employ actuaries.

The Regulation of Financial Services.q: At the global level, which body coordinates anti-money laundering and counter-terrorist financing standards?
o: Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development
The Regulation of Financial Services.w: The Financial Action Task Force sets international standards to combat money laundering and terrorist financing.

n.0: The Basel Committee on Banking Supervision issues banking capital standards, not AML.
n.1: The International Monetary Fund promotes global stability, not AML.
n.3: The Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development supports economic policy, not AML.

The Regulation of Financial Services.q: At the international level, which body identifies and monitors global systemically important banks (G-SIBs)?
The Regulation of Financial Services.w: The Financial Stability Board identifies and monitors global systemically important banks and recommends regulatory policies.

n.1: The Basel Committee on Banking Supervision develops bank capital standards, not G-SIB monitoring.
n.2: The International Organization of Securities Commissions focuses on securities, not G-SIBs.
n.3: The International Monetary Fund promotes stability but does not designate G-SIBs.

The Regulation of Financial Services.q: Who is responsible for setting the UK’s overall economic strategy?
The Regulation of Financial Services.w: HM Treasury is responsible for fiscal and economic strategy, working with regulators to align it with government policy.

n.1: The FCA regulates conduct, not economic strategy.
n.2: The PRA supervises prudential risks.
n.3: The FPC targets systemic risk.

The Regulation of Financial Services.q: Which international body coordinates global AML and CTF measures?
o: Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development
The Regulation of Financial Services.w: The Financial Action Task Force coordinates global efforts against money laundering and terrorist financing, issuing recommendations adopted worldwide.

n.1: The Basel Committee sets banking capital standards, not AML measures.
n.2: IOSCO sets securities standards, not AML measures.
n.3: The OECD advises on economic policy, not AML frameworks.

The Regulation of Financial Services.q: Which organisation works to ensure that auditors remain independent from the companies whose accounts they audit?
The Regulation of Financial Services.w: The Financial Reporting Council safeguards auditor independence, protecting the credibility of corporate audits.

n.0: The Financial Conduct Authority oversees market conduct, not auditor independence.
n.1: The Prudential Regulation Authority supervises prudential soundness, not auditors.
n.3: The Competition and Markets Authority addresses competition, not auditor independence.

The Regulation of Financial Services.q: What is the role of the Takeover Panel?
o: Overseeing compliance with the Takeover Code
The Regulation of Financial Services.w: The Takeover Panel administers and enforces the UK Takeover Code, ensuring fair treatment of shareholders in mergers and acquisitions.

n.0: Insurer solvency is a PRA responsibility.
n.2: The FCA enforces conduct rules.
n.3: Monetary policy is set by the MPC.

The Regulation of Financial Services.q: Across the financial services sector, which regulator is responsible for enforcing UK data protection law?
The Regulation of Financial Services.w: The Information Commissioner's Office enforces data protection and privacy law across all sectors, including financial services.

n.0: The Financial Conduct Authority regulates conduct, not data protection law.
n.1: The Prudential Regulation Authority supervises prudential risks, not privacy.
n.2: The Competition and Markets Authority enforces competition law, not data protection.

The Regulation of Financial Services.q: Which body is responsible for investigating complaints about the administration of occupational pension schemes?
The Regulation of Financial Services.w: The Pensions Ombudsman resolves complaints about how occupational schemes are administered and disputes with trustees.

n.1: The Financial Ombudsman Service resolves consumer disputes, not occupational pensions.
n.2: The Pensions Regulator supervises governance but does not handle complaints.
n.3: The Prudential Regulation Authority supervises prudential safety, not administration.

The Regulation of Financial Services.q: What is the FSCS’s relationship with the PRA and FCA?
o: It is accountable to both regulators
It directly regulates banks and insurers
It sets capital requirements for firms
The Regulation of Financial Services.w: The Financial Services Compensation Scheme is accountable to both the PRA and the FCA, providing consumer protection through compensation.

n.1: The FSCS compensates claimants rather than regulating firms.
n.2: Capital requirements are set by the PRA.
n.3: Authorisation is handled by the PRA or FCA.

The Regulation of Financial Services.q: Which body oversees occupational pension schemes in the UK?
The Regulation of Financial Services.w: The Pensions Regulator oversees occupational pension schemes, ensuring trustees meet their governance and funding responsibilities.

n.0: The FCA regulates personal pensions and conduct.
n.1: The Bank oversees systemic risks.
n.3: The CMA focuses on competition.

The Regulation of Financial Services.q: Which body investigates serious insider dealing beyond routine FCA enforcement?
The Regulation of Financial Services.w: The Serious Fraud Office investigates and prosecutes serious or complex fraud and insider dealing beyond routine FCA enforcement.

n.1: The FRC oversees reporting and auditing.
n.2: The Bank focuses on systemic risks.
n.3: The CMA deals with competition issues.

The Regulation of Financial Services.q: Which FCA power allows it to stop misleading financial promotions immediately?
The Regulation of Financial Services.w: The FCA can use its temporary product intervention power to ban or restrict promotions and products that risk consumer detriment.

n.0: The countercyclical buffer is a macroprudential tool set by the FPC.
n.1: A Section 166 review examines specific areas of a firm.
n.2: Resolution powers are executed by the Bank of England.

The Regulation of Financial Services.q: Which EU directive strengthened bank capital and liquidity standards in the wake of the crisis?
The Regulation of Financial Services.w: CRD IV transposed Basel III requirements into EU law, strengthening banks' capital and liquidity standards.

n.0: The MiFID II Directive focuses on conduct, not capital.
n.1: The UCITS Directive governs funds, not bank capital.
n.2: The Solvency II Directive applies to insurers, not banks.

The Regulation of Financial Services.q: Which EU directive sets the harmonised prudential rules that apply to insurers across member states?
The Regulation of Financial Services.w: The Solvency II Directive establishes harmonised rules for insurance regulation, covering solvency, capital and risk management.

n.0: The MiFID II Directive regulates markets and investor protection, not insurers.
n.2: The UCITS Directive governs investment funds, not insurers.
n.3: The Payment Services Directive regulates payments, not insurance solvency.

The Regulation of Financial Services.q: Which body oversees the professional standards of accountants in the UK?
The Regulation of Financial Services.w: The ICAEW regulates its members and sets professional standards for accountants in England and Wales.

n.1: The FCA regulates conduct in financial markets, not accountants.
n.2: The PRA regulates prudential safety.
n.3: The Bank of England manages systemic risks.

The Regulation of Financial Services.q: Within the UK regulatory framework, what is the main role performed by the Financial Ombudsman Service?
The Regulation of Financial Services.w: The Financial Ombudsman Service provides impartial dispute resolution for consumers and financial firms outside the courts.

n.0: Capital requirements are set by the PRA.
n.1: Trustees are overseen by The Pensions Regulator.
n.2: Data protection is enforced by the ICO.

The Regulation of Financial Services.q: Which professional body oversees the conduct and competence of practising barristers in England and Wales?
The Regulation of Financial Services.w: The Bar Standards Board regulates barristers, ensuring their professional conduct and competence.

n.0: The Solicitors Regulation Authority regulates solicitors, not barristers.
n.2: The Institute and Faculty of Actuaries regulates actuaries, not barristers.
n.3: The Competition and Markets Authority enforces competition law, not barristers' conduct.

The Regulation of Financial Services.q: Which EU directive created the investor protection and conduct of business rules for investment firms?
The Regulation of Financial Services.w: MiFID II created comprehensive investor protection and conduct rules for investment firms, improving transparency and consumer safeguards.

n.0: The Solvency II Directive applies to insurers, not investor conduct.
n.1: The UCITS Directive governs funds, not conduct broadly.
n.3: The Payment Services Directive regulates payments, not investor conduct.

The Regulation of Financial Services.q: What is the PRA’s primary statutory objective?
o: Ensure the best possible consumer outcomes
The Regulation of Financial Services.w: The PRA’s core objective is to promote the safety and soundness of the firms it regulates.

n.1: Consumer outcomes are the FCA’s conduct focus.
n.2: Low, stable inflation is targeted by the MPC.
n.3: Competition sits mainly with the FCA.

The Regulation of Financial Services.q: Which global agreement set the minimum international standards for bank capital, liquidity and leverage?
The Regulation of Financial Services.w: Basel III sets global standards on bank capital, liquidity and leverage, implemented regionally through directives such as CRD IV.

n.1: The MiFID II Directive covers investor protection, not bank capital.
n.2: The Solvency II Directive applies to insurers, not banks.
n.3: The PRIIPs Regulation covers retail disclosure, not bank capital.

The Regulation of Financial Services.q: Which body took over consumer credit regulation after the transfer from the OFT?
The Regulation of Financial Services.w: Consumer credit regulation transferred from the Office of Fair Trading to the FCA in 2014, which now authorises and supervises the sector.

n.0: The PRA focuses on prudential soundness.
n.1: The Bank oversees monetary and systemic stability.
n.2: The CMA handles competition.

The Regulation of Financial Services.q: Which body provides independent oversight of the corporate reporting produced by listed companies in the UK?
The Regulation of Financial Services.w: The FRC monitors corporate reporting of listed companies to maintain transparency and investor confidence.

n.0: The Financial Conduct Authority enforces conduct but not detailed reporting standards.
n.1: The Competition and Markets Authority enforces competition, not reporting standards.
n.2: The Prudential Regulation Authority supervises prudential safety, not reporting.

The Regulation of Financial Services.q: What did the second Payment Services Directive (PSD2) introduce into the EU regulatory framework?
The Regulation of Financial Services.w: PSD2 introduced open banking, requiring banks to give third parties access to payment accounts to encourage competition.

n.0: Insurance prudential rules are in Solvency II.
n.1: Bank capital is covered by Basel and CRD.
n.3: Governance codes are separate from payment rules.

The Regulation of Financial Services.q: Who decides the authorisation of a new UK bank?
The Regulation of Financial Services.w: Dual-regulated firms such as banks are authorised by the PRA with the FCA’s consent on conduct matters.

n.0: The FCA cannot authorise a bank alone.
n.2: The Court oversees Bank governance, not authorisations.
n.3: The CMA handles competition, not authorisation.

The Regulation of Financial Services.q: Which Bank of England committee is responsible for prudential regulation policy?
The Regulation of Financial Services.w: The Prudential Regulation Committee oversees the PRA’s prudential regulation policy, ensuring banks and insurers are safe and sound.

n.0: The FPC addresses systemic risks, not firm-level policy.
n.2: The MPC manages inflation and interest rates.
n.3: The Court is the Bank’s governing board.

The Regulation of Financial Services.q: Which government body is responsible for overseeing insolvency practitioners and director disqualifications in the UK?
The Regulation of Financial Services.w: The Insolvency Service oversees insolvency practitioners and director disqualifications, ensuring the insolvency regime operates properly.

n.0: The Financial Conduct Authority regulates conduct, not insolvency practitioners.
n.2: The Financial Reporting Council sets audit standards, not insolvency rules.
n.3: The Prudential Regulation Authority regulates prudential risks, not insolvency.

The Regulation of Financial Services.q: How does the Bank of England support solvent banks during liquidity stress?
o: It imposes sales conduct restrictions on them
It sets mandatory product value metrics
It grants them premium listing approvals
The Regulation of Financial Services.w: The Bank of England provides liquidity through lender-of-last-resort facilities to solvent firms.

n.1: Sales conduct restrictions are FCA measures.
n.2: Product value metrics relate to FCA consumer outcomes.
n.3: Listing approvals are an FCA responsibility.

The Regulation of Financial Services.q: Which UK body is responsible for setting the governance standards that occupational pension schemes must meet?
The Regulation of Financial Services.w: The Pensions Regulator ensures occupational pension schemes have proper governance, protecting members' benefits.

n.1: The Financial Conduct Authority oversees personal pension conduct, not occupational governance.
n.2: The Competition and Markets Authority enforces competition, not pension governance.
n.3: The Financial Reporting Council oversees reporting and audit, not scheme governance.

The Regulation of Financial Services.q: Which EU directive requires member states to maintain investor compensation schemes protecting clients of failed firms?
The Regulation of Financial Services.w: The Investor Compensation Schemes Directive requires member states to protect investors where firms fail to return assets.

n.0: The MiFID II Directive governs markets and conduct, not compensation.
n.1: The UCITS Directive covers collective funds, not compensation.
n.2: The Solvency II Directive applies to insurers, not compensation.

The Regulation of Financial Services.q: Which FCA division operates the UK Listing Authority function?
The Regulation of Financial Services.w: The FCA’s Markets division operates the UK Listing Authority function, overseeing issuers, disclosure and market integrity.

n.0: Resolution is the Bank’s remit.
n.1: The PRA’s prudential division supervises firm safety.
n.3: Competition matters sit mainly with the CMA.

The Regulation of Financial Services.q: Which professional body is responsible for regulating the professional conduct of actuaries in the UK?
The Regulation of Financial Services.w: The Institute and Faculty of Actuaries regulates actuaries' professional conduct, education and ethics in the UK.

n.0: The Financial Reporting Council sets reporting and audit standards, not actuaries.
n.1: The Financial Conduct Authority regulates firms' conduct, not actuaries.
n.3: The Prudential Regulation Authority supervises firms, not individual professionals.

The Regulation of Financial Services.q: What does the FCA’s competition objective require it to do?
o: Maximise profits for the financial firms
Guarantee market stability at all times
The Regulation of Financial Services.w: The FCA’s competition objective requires it to promote effective competition in the interests of consumers, improving choice and outcomes.

n.1: Objectives are not designed to maximise firm profits.
n.2: Market stability is a Bank of England role.
n.3: Bond issuance is managed by the DMO.

The Regulation of Financial Services.q: What is the PRA’s approach to setting requirements for an insurer’s own funds?
o: Risk-based standards aligned to Solvency II
A uniform leverage ratio identical to retail banks
Product intervention capping premiums for vulnerable customers
The Regulation of Financial Services.w: For insurers the PRA applies a risk-based prudential regime aligned to Solvency II concepts, focusing on policyholder protection and firm soundness.

n.1: A bank-style leverage ratio is not applied uniformly to insurers.
n.2: Premium caps are a conduct matter.
n.3: Monetary policy tools sit with the MPC.

The Regulation of Financial Services.q: At the international level, which standard-setter is responsible for issuing the Basel banking accords?
o: Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development
The Regulation of Financial Services.w: The Basel Committee on Banking Supervision issues the Basel Accords, setting international standards for bank capital and risk.

n.1: The International Monetary Fund supports global stability but issues no accords.
n.2: The European Central Bank sets eurozone monetary policy, not prudential standards.
n.3: The Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development focuses on economic policy, not banking regulation.

The Regulation of Financial Services.q: Which Bank of England committee identifies systemic risks and takes macroprudential action?
The Regulation of Financial Services.w: The Financial Policy Committee identifies systemic risks and implements macroprudential policy to safeguard financial stability.

n.0: The PRC handles firm-level prudential supervision.
n.2: The MPC focuses on inflation and interest rates.
n.3: The Risk and Audit Committee oversees internal Bank controls.

The Regulation of Financial Services.q: Which UK Act converted retained EU financial law into domestic law after Brexit?
The Regulation of Financial Services.w: The European Union (Withdrawal) Act 2018 converted EU law, including financial directives, into UK domestic law after Brexit.

n.0: The Financial Services and Markets Act 2000 provides the framework but not the Brexit mechanism.
n.1: The Banking Act 2009 deals with resolution powers, not EU law.
n.3: The Companies Act 2006 governs company law, not EU withdrawal.

The Regulation of Financial Services.q: Which Bank of England body sets system-wide macroprudential policy?
o: The Court of the Bank of England
The Regulation of Financial Services.w: Macroprudential policy, such as sectoral capital requirements and the countercyclical buffer, is set by the Financial Policy Committee to address system-wide risks.

n.0: The PRC oversees firm-level prudential regulation.
n.2: The MPC targets price stability through monetary policy.
n.3: The Court is the Bank’s governing board.

The Regulation of Financial Services.q: Which UK Act gave statutory effect to ring-fencing of retail and investment banking?
The Regulation of Financial Services.w: The Financial Services (Banking Reform) Act 2013 gave statutory effect to ring-fencing, separating retail from riskier investment banking.

n.0: The Financial Services Act 2012 created the FCA and PRA but not ring-fencing.
n.2: The Banking Act 2009 introduced resolution powers, not ring-fencing.
n.3: The Companies Act 2006 governs company law, not ring-fencing.

The Regulation of Financial Services.q: Which organisation investigates company insolvencies in the UK?
The Regulation of Financial Services.w: The Insolvency Service investigates insolvencies and director misconduct, supporting the UK insolvency regime.

n.0: The FCA regulates conduct, not insolvency.
n.1: The PRA supervises financial soundness.
n.2: The CMA deals with competition.

The Regulation of Financial Services.q: Which body oversees monetary stability in the UK?
The Regulation of Financial Services.w: The Bank of England’s Monetary Policy Committee manages monetary stability, mainly by setting interest rates to control inflation.

n.0: The FCA oversees conduct and market integrity.
n.1: The PRA manages prudential soundness.
n.2: The CMA enforces competition policy.

The Regulation of Financial Services.q: Who prosecutes market misconduct that amounts to serious criminal fraud beyond FCA enforcement?
The Regulation of Financial Services.w: The Serious Fraud Office can prosecute market misconduct where it constitutes serious criminal fraud beyond FCA regulatory action.

n.0: The Information Commissioner's Office enforces data protection, not financial crime.
n.2: The Financial Reporting Council regulates audits and reporting, not market crime.
n.3: The Prudential Regulation Authority focuses on prudential supervision, not criminal law.

The Regulation of Financial Services.q: Within the UK, which regulator is responsible for monitoring competition in wholesale financial markets?
The Regulation of Financial Services.w: The CMA investigates and enforces competition issues across all markets, including wholesale financial markets.

n.0: The Financial Conduct Authority enforces conduct rules, not competition law.
n.2: The Prudential Regulation Authority ensures prudential soundness, not competition.
n.3: The Financial Ombudsman Service handles disputes, not market competition.

The Regulation of Financial Services.q: Which EU measure harmonises rules for packaged retail and insurance-based investment products?

n.0: The MiFID II Directive governs market conduct, not PRIIPs disclosure.
n.1: The UCITS Directive applies to collective funds, not PRIIPs broadly.
n.3: The Solvency II Directive covers insurers' prudential rules, not disclosure.

The Regulation of Financial Services.q: What is the FCA’s role in relation to market abuse?
o: Setting monetary policy to reduce it
Providing emergency liquidity in such cases
The Regulation of Financial Services.w: The FCA enforces the Market Abuse Regulation by investigating misconduct and imposing penalties to maintain market integrity.

n.0: Monetary policy does not address market abuse.
n.1: Liquidity support is the Bank’s role.
n.2: Debt issuance is managed by the DMO.

The Regulation of Financial Services.q: What action may HM Treasury take in relation to regulators to protect public funds?
o: Direct the FCA to impose immediate misconduct fines
Appoint new senior managers within firms
Issue directions on resolution tools using public money
Mandate the PRA to waive capital requirements
The Regulation of Financial Services.w: HM Treasury may direct regulators, particularly the Bank, where public funds are involved in resolution or support measures.

n.0: Enforcement fines are the FCA’s responsibility.
n.1: Appointments within firms fall under the SMCR.
n.3: Capital requirements are set by regulators, not waived by Treasury.

The Regulation of Financial Services.q: Which EU directive sets the harmonised prudential standards that apply to insurers across member states?
The Regulation of Financial Services.w: The Solvency II Directive provides harmonised prudential regulation for insurers, covering capital, governance and risk management.

n.1: The MiFID II Directive regulates investment firm conduct, not insurers.
n.2: The UCITS Directive covers collective schemes, not insurers.
n.3: The Bank Recovery and Resolution Directive applies to banks, not insurers.

The Regulation of Financial Services.q: Which EU regulation introduced transparency rules and restrictions covering short-selling activities in the markets?
The Regulation of Financial Services.w: The EU Short Selling Regulation introduced transparency and restrictions on uncovered short-selling to improve market integrity.

n.0: The MiFID II Directive covers conduct rules, not short-selling transparency.
n.2: The UCITS Directive governs collective schemes, not short-selling.
n.3: The Payment Services Directive regulates payments, not short-selling.

The Regulation of Financial Services.q: Following the FSMA reforms, what additional objective do the FCA and PRA share?
o: A joint duty to set interest rates in crises
A primary objective to maximise fee income
A secondary objective on growth and competitiveness
A duty to approve all large mergers

n.0: Interest-rate setting remains with the MPC.
n.1: Objectives are not framed around fee income.
n.3: Merger control sits mainly with the CMA.

The Regulation of Financial Services.q: Within the UK, which regulator is responsible for monitoring the auditors of listed companies?
The Regulation of Financial Services.w: The FRC oversees the regulation and monitoring of auditors to maintain standards in listed company audits.

n.0: The Financial Conduct Authority enforces market conduct, not audit oversight.
n.2: The Prudential Regulation Authority supervises prudential soundness, not auditors.
n.3: The Competition and Markets Authority enforces competition law, not audit monitoring.

The Regulation of Financial Services.q: Which UK Act gave regulators stronger powers to ring-fence retail banking operations?
The Regulation of Financial Services.w: The Financial Services (Banking Reform) Act 2013 implemented ring-fencing of retail from investment banking to reduce systemic risk.

n.0: The Financial Services and Markets Act 2000 is the overarching framework, not ring-fencing.
n.1: The Companies Act 2006 governs company law, not ring-fencing.
n.2: The Banking Act 2009 established resolution tools, not ring-fencing.

The Regulation of Financial Services.q: Which EU regulation introduced uniform rules governing the administration of financial benchmarks across member states?
The Regulation of Financial Services.w: The EU Benchmarks Regulation created standards for benchmark administrators to enhance transparency and reduce manipulation.
