n.3: The Solvency II Directive applies to insurers, not benchmarks.

The Regulation of Financial Services.q: Which professional body sets the professional and ethical standards governing actuaries working in the UK?
The Regulation of Financial Services.w: The Institute and Faculty of Actuaries sets professional and ethical standards for the actuarial profession in the UK.

n.0: The Financial Reporting Council oversees audit and reporting, not actuarial ethics.
n.1: The Financial Conduct Authority regulates market conduct, not actuarial ethics.
n.3: The Prudential Regulation Authority supervises firms, not actuaries.

The Regulation of Financial Services.q: Within the UK, which organisation is responsible for investigating serious cases of accounting and audit misconduct?
The Regulation of Financial Services.w: The Financial Reporting Council investigates serious accounting and audit misconduct to uphold trust in corporate reporting.

n.0: The Financial Conduct Authority focuses on market conduct, not accounting.
n.1: The Prudential Regulation Authority ensures financial soundness, not accounting.
n.2: The Competition and Markets Authority enforces competition policy, not accounting.

The Regulation of Financial Services.q: Who prosecutes offences under the UK Bribery Act arising in financial services?
The Regulation of Financial Services.w: The Serious Fraud Office prosecutes serious criminal offences under the Bribery Act, including in financial services.

n.0: The Financial Conduct Authority enforces conduct rules, not criminal bribery.
n.1: The Competition and Markets Authority enforces competition, not bribery law.
n.2: The Information Commissioner's Office enforces data protection, not bribery.

The Regulation of Financial Services.q: Which EU directive harmonises the conduct of business standards applying to investment firms across member states?
The Regulation of Financial Services.w: MiFID II harmonises conduct standards across EU investment firms, ensuring transparency and investor protection.

n.1: The Solvency II Directive governs insurers, not investment firm conduct.
n.2: The UCITS Directive regulates funds, not investment firms.
n.3: The Bank Recovery and Resolution Directive covers bank recovery, not conduct standards.

The Regulation of Financial Services.q: Which role does HM Treasury play in relation to financial regulation?
o: It issues individual prudential capital requirements
It sets the framework for the regulators
It determines stock exchange listing requirements
The Regulation of Financial Services.w: HM Treasury sets the statutory and policy framework within which the regulators operate, providing strategic direction and accountability.

n.0: Supervising firm conduct is the FCA’s role.
n.1: Capital requirements are set by the PRA.
n.3: Listing rules are administered by the FCA.

The Regulation of Financial Services.q: Within the UK financial system, which body supervises the application of competition law to retail banking services?
The Regulation of Financial Services.w: The Competition and Markets Authority investigates and acts against anti-competitive practices, including in retail banking.

n.1: The Financial Conduct Authority regulates conduct and disclosure, not competition law.
n.2: The Prudential Regulation Authority oversees prudential soundness, not competition.
n.3: The Information Commissioner's Office enforces data protection, not competition.

The Regulation of Financial Services.q: Which UK authority was responsible for transposing EU directives into national law pre-Brexit?
The Regulation of Financial Services.w: HM Treasury had responsibility for transposing EU directives into UK law, working with regulators on detailed rules.

n.1: The Financial Conduct Authority applies directives but does not transpose them.
n.2: The Prudential Regulation Authority supervises firms, not legislative transposition.
n.3: The Competition and Markets Authority enforces competition, not transposition.

The Regulation of Financial Services.q: Who enforces the UK’s Competition Act 1998 in financial markets?
The Regulation of Financial Services.w: The Competition and Markets Authority enforces the Competition Act 1998, including in financial services, to prevent anti-competitive practices.

n.0: The FCA regulates conduct, not the Competition Act.
n.1: The PRA focuses on prudential safety.
n.3: The FSCS pays compensation to consumers.

The Regulation of Financial Services.q: At the international level, which organisation coordinates global financial stability initiatives across jurisdictions?
The Regulation of Financial Services.w: The Financial Stability Board coordinates internationally to monitor and make recommendations about the global financial system.

n.1: The International Organization of Securities Commissions sets securities standards, not overall stability.
n.2: The Basel Committee on Banking Supervision sets bank standards, not overall coordination.
n.3: The International Monetary Fund supports stability but the FSB coordinates globally.

The Regulation of Financial Services.q: Which regulator is primarily concerned with ensuring the fair treatment of customers?
The Regulation of Financial Services.w: The FCA is the conduct regulator, and its remit includes ensuring the fair treatment of customers across financial services.

n.0: The PRA focuses on prudential soundness.
n.1: The Bank covers monetary and systemic stability.
n.3: The FPC addresses system-wide risks.

The Regulation of Financial Services.q: Which EU regulation governs transparency requirements for securities financing transactions such as repos and lending?
The Regulation of Financial Services.w: The SFTR introduced transparency rules for securities lending and repos, requiring reporting to trade repositories.

n.0: The MiFID II Directive governs conduct rules, not securities financing.
n.1: The UCITS Directive governs collective schemes, not securities financing.
n.3: The Solvency II Directive applies to insurers, not repo markets.

The Regulation of Financial Services.q: What is the Bank of England’s resolution objective under the Banking Act 2009?
o: Guaranteeing the profitability of failing banks
The Regulation of Financial Services.w: The Bank’s resolution objective is to protect and enhance financial stability while minimising public costs and maintaining critical services.

n.0: Resolution does not guarantee profitability.
n.2: Consumer protection is the FCA’s remit.
n.3: Borrowing is managed by HM Treasury and the DMO.

The Regulation of Financial Services.q: Which body monitors UK financial reporting and accounting standards?
The Regulation of Financial Services.w: The Financial Reporting Council oversees corporate reporting, audit quality and actuarial standards in the UK.

n.0: The FCA supervises conduct, not accounting standards.
n.1: The Bank focuses on monetary and systemic stability.
n.2: The CMA enforces competition law.

The Regulation of Financial Services.q: Which EU directive harmonises fund management and enables cross-border distribution of funds across member states?
The Regulation of Financial Services.w: The UCITS Directive harmonises fund regulation, enabling cross-border distribution of mutual funds in the EU.

n.0: The Solvency II Directive applies to insurers, not funds.
n.1: The MiFID II Directive regulates markets, not collective investments.
n.3: The Payment Services Directive regulates payments, not funds.

The Regulation of Financial Services.q: Which UK body ensures compliance with advertising rules in print and digital media?
The Regulation of Financial Services.w: The Advertising Standards Authority regulates print and digital advertising, ensuring promotions are not misleading.

n.0: The Financial Conduct Authority regulates promotions but relies on the ASA for ad standards.
n.1: The Prudential Regulation Authority oversees prudential soundness, not advertising.
n.3: The Competition and Markets Authority enforces competition, not advertising standards.

The Regulation of Financial Services.q: Which body supervises accountancy service providers for compliance with the UK anti-money laundering regime?
The Regulation of Financial Services.w: HMRC supervises certain sectors, including accountancy service providers, for compliance with the UK anti-money laundering regime.

n.0: The Financial Reporting Council sets reporting and audit standards, not AML.
n.1: The Financial Conduct Authority regulates financial firms, not accountancy AML.
n.2: The Competition and Markets Authority enforces competition law, not AML compliance.

The Regulation of Financial Services.q: Which Bank of England function supports market stability during liquidity shortages?
The Regulation of Financial Services.w: The Bank of England acts as lender of last resort, providing liquidity to solvent firms to maintain market stability.

n.1: Skilled person reviews are supervisory tools.
n.2: Redress schemes are FCA tools.
n.3: Listing waivers are an FCA function.

The Regulation of Financial Services.q: Which regulator oversees auditors and audit quality in the UK?
The Regulation of Financial Services.w: The Financial Reporting Council regulates auditors and monitors audit quality to promote high standards of corporate governance.

n.0: The FCA oversees financial markets conduct.
n.1: The CMA enforces competition law.
n.3: The Bank focuses on systemic stability.

The Regulation of Financial Services.q: Which statutory body has oversight of the funding standards applying to UK occupational pension schemes?
The Regulation of Financial Services.w: The Pensions Regulator ensures occupational pension schemes are funded appropriately to protect members' benefits.

n.1: The Financial Conduct Authority focuses on market conduct, not pension funding.
n.2: The Prudential Regulation Authority supervises insurers and banks, not schemes.
n.3: The Financial Reporting Council oversees reporting and audit, not pension funding.

The Regulation of Financial Services.q: What is the purpose of the EU Capital Requirements Directive (CRD IV)?
o: Implement Basel III in EU law
The Regulation of Financial Services.w: CRD IV transposed Basel III banking standards into EU law, including capital adequacy, liquidity and leverage requirements.

n.0: Open banking was introduced by PSD2.
n.1: Investor protection is MiFID II's focus.
n.3: Insurance solvency is covered by Solvency II.

The Regulation of Financial Services.q: What is the FCA’s general duty when proposing significant Handbook changes?
o: Seek HM Treasury approval before any consultation
Publish rules without consultation if pro-competitive
Refer the proposals to the PRC for prudential sign-off
Carry out cost-benefit analysis and consult
The Regulation of Financial Services.w: The FCA’s rule-making powers require a cost-benefit analysis and consultation before making significant rules, subject to limited exceptions.

n.0: Treasury approval is not a blanket prerequisite.
n.1: Competition benefits do not remove the consultation duty.
n.2: The PRC does not sign off FCA conduct rules.

The Regulation of Financial Services.q: Which UK legislation created the Prudential Regulation Authority and Financial Conduct Authority?
The Regulation of Financial Services.w: The Financial Services Act 2012 abolished the FSA and created the FCA and PRA within the twin-peaks model.

n.0: The Banking Act 2009 introduced resolution powers, not FCA/PRA.
n.1: The Companies Act 2006 governs company law, not regulators.
n.2: The Financial Services and Markets Act 2000 created the FSA, later replaced by the 2012 Act.

The Regulation of Financial Services.q: Who issues the statutory ‘remit and recommendations’ letters guiding the regulators’ priorities?
o: The FCA Board, to the PRA and Bank committees
The Bank of England’s Court, to HM Treasury
The Competition and Markets Authority, to the FCA
HM Treasury, to the FCA, PRA and Bank committees
The Regulation of Financial Services.w: HM Treasury periodically sends remit and recommendations letters setting strategic priorities for the FCA, PRA and certain Bank committees.

n.0: The FCA receives such guidance rather than issuing it.
n.1: The Court manages Bank governance.
n.2: The CMA does not issue Treasury remits.

The Regulation of Financial Services.q: Which EU directive requires banks to prepare and maintain recovery and resolution plans for potential failure?
The Regulation of Financial Services.w: The Bank Recovery and Resolution Directive requires banks to prepare recovery and resolution plans to manage potential failures.

n.1: The MiFID II Directive regulates securities markets, not resolution.
n.2: The Solvency II Directive applies to insurers, not banks.
n.3: The Payment Services Directive covers payments, not bank resolution.

The Regulation of Financial Services.q: Under UK law, which regulator is responsible for overseeing the regulation of consumer credit agreements?
The Regulation of Financial Services.w: The FCA regulates consumer credit, ensuring agreements are fair and firms treat customers appropriately.

n.0: The Prudential Regulation Authority oversees prudential risks, not consumer credit.
n.1: The Competition and Markets Authority enforces competition, not consumer credit law.
n.3: The Financial Reporting Council oversees reporting, not credit regulation.

The Regulation of Financial Services.q: Which Bank of England committee’s decisions most directly affect consumer mortgage rates?
The Regulation of Financial Services.w: The Monetary Policy Committee’s decisions on the Bank Rate directly influence borrowing costs, including mortgage rates.

n.0: The FPC manages systemic risks.
n.2: The PRC focuses on prudential policy.
n.3: The Court oversees Bank governance.

The Regulation of Financial Services.q: When must the FCA consult on changes to the Listing Rules?
o: Only after HM Treasury approval is granted
Only after a firm requests a consultation
The Regulation of Financial Services.w: Under its rule-making powers, the FCA generally consults before making significant Listing Rule changes.

n.0: Treasury approval is not a prerequisite for consultation.
n.1: Consultation is not limited to emergencies.
n.2: Consultations follow FCA proposals, not firm requests.

The Regulation of Financial Services.q: Which EU measure requires standardised disclosure documents for packaged retail investment products sold to consumers?
The Regulation of Financial Services.w: The PRIIPs Regulation requires standardised disclosure documents to help retail investors compare packaged products.

n.0: The MiFID II Directive governs conduct, not PRIIPs disclosure.
n.2: The UCITS Directive governs funds but PRIIPs applies more broadly.
n.3: The Solvency II Directive applies to insurers, not disclosure.

The Regulation of Financial Services.q: Which professional body sets the ethical and educational standards for the insurance broking profession in the UK?
The Regulation of Financial Services.w: The Chartered Insurance Institute is the professional body setting ethical and educational standards for brokers and advisers.

n.0: The Financial Conduct Authority regulates broker conduct, not professional standards.
n.1: The Prudential Regulation Authority supervises insurer solvency, not brokers' conduct.
n.3: The Competition and Markets Authority enforces competition law, not professional standards.

The Regulation of Financial Services.q: Which body provides independent dispute resolution for complaints relating to occupational pension schemes in the UK?
The Regulation of Financial Services.w: The Pensions Ombudsman investigates and resolves complaints about pensions administration and trustee decisions.

n.0: The Financial Ombudsman Service handles consumer disputes, not occupational pensions.
n.2: The Pensions Regulator oversees schemes but does not resolve disputes.
n.3: The Financial Reporting Council handles reporting, not pension complaints.

The Regulation of Financial Services.q: Which independent body provides redress for consumers who are in dispute with their financial advisers over advice?
The Regulation of Financial Services.w: The Financial Ombudsman Service provides impartial redress for adviser-consumer disputes, avoiding court processes.

n.1: The Pensions Ombudsman handles occupational pension complaints, not adviser disputes.
n.2: The Financial Conduct Authority regulates adviser conduct but offers no redress.
n.3: The Prudential Regulation Authority ensures prudential soundness, not disputes.

The Regulation of Financial Services.q: Which body is responsible for prosecuting insider trading where it constitutes a serious criminal offence?
The Regulation of Financial Services.w: The Serious Fraud Office investigates and prosecutes insider trading where it amounts to serious criminal activity.

n.0: The Financial Conduct Authority enforces civil sanctions, but serious crimes go to the SFO.
n.1: The Prudential Regulation Authority regulates prudential soundness, not criminal cases.
n.3: The Insolvency Service investigates insolvencies, not insider trading.

The Regulation of Financial Services.q: Within the insurance sector, which regulator investigates suspected anti-competitive pricing practices between firms?
The Regulation of Financial Services.w: The CMA enforces competition law across sectors, including investigations into anti-competitive pricing in insurance.

n.0: The Financial Conduct Authority regulates conduct and outcomes, not competition.
n.1: The Prudential Regulation Authority ensures prudential safety, not competition.
n.2: The Financial Ombudsman Service resolves disputes, not competition issues.

The Regulation of Financial Services.q: Which directive harmonises investor protection and conduct standards across Europe?
The Regulation of Financial Services.w: MiFID II harmonises investor protection and conduct standards across EU financial markets.

n.0: Solvency II governs insurers, not investor conduct.
n.1: UCITS regulates investment funds, not investor conduct broadly.
n.3: PSD2 governs payments, not investor conduct.

The Regulation of Financial Services.q: Which international agreement set the reform commitments for over-the-counter derivatives markets after the financial crisis?
The Regulation of Financial Services.w: The G20 Pittsburgh Summit in 2009 agreed reforms to OTC derivatives, including mandatory clearing and reporting.

n.1: The OECD Principles of Corporate Governance focus on company boards, not derivatives.
n.2: The IMF Special Drawing Rights framework relate to currency reserves, not derivatives.
n.3: The Basel II Accord covers bank capital, not derivatives.

The Regulation of Financial Services.q: What role does the PRA play within the Bank of England’s overall structure?
o: It is the Bank’s prudential regulatory arm
It sets fiscal policy for the government
It administers conduct rules for all investment firms
The Regulation of Financial Services.w: The PRA operates as part of the Bank of England, acting as prudential regulator for banks, insurers and systemic firms, overseen by the PRC.

n.1: Fiscal policy is managed by HM Treasury.
n.2: Conduct rules for investment firms are an FCA responsibility.
n.3: Debt issuance is managed by the DMO.

The Regulation of Financial Services.q: Within the UK financial sector, which authority is responsible for investigating suspected cartel behaviour between firms?
The Regulation of Financial Services.w: The CMA investigates and takes enforcement action against cartel behaviour across sectors, including financial services.

n.0: The Financial Conduct Authority regulates conduct but does not lead cartel enforcement.
n.2: The Prudential Regulation Authority regulates prudential safety, not cartels.
n.3: The Financial Ombudsman Service resolves disputes, not cartel investigations.

The Regulation of Financial Services.q: Which UK Act provides the main statutory framework for financial services regulation?
The Regulation of Financial Services.w: The Financial Services and Markets Act 2000 establishes the statutory basis for regulation, underpinning the powers of the FCA and PRA.

n.0: The Banking Act 2009 introduced resolution powers, not the main framework.
n.2: The Companies Act 2006 governs company law, not regulation.
n.3: The Financial Services (Banking Reform) Act 2013 introduced ring-fencing, not the main framework.

The Regulation of Financial Services.q: Which UK body enforces data protection laws relevant to financial firms?
The Regulation of Financial Services.w: The Information Commissioner’s Office enforces UK data protection laws, including the UK GDPR and Data Protection Act, across all sectors.

n.0: The FCA focuses on conduct, not data protection.
n.2: The Bank of England manages stability.
n.3: The PRA supervises prudential safety.

The Regulation of Financial Services.q: Which EU directive harmonises bank capital requirements by implementing Basel standards across member states?
The Regulation of Financial Services.w: The Capital Requirements Directive implements Basel standards in EU law, harmonising capital adequacy across member states.

n.0: The Solvency II Directive applies to insurers, not banks.
n.1: The UCITS Directive covers investment funds, not bank capital.
n.3: The MiFID II Directive regulates conduct, not capital.

The Regulation of Financial Services.q: Which EU directive regulates electronic money institutions, covering issuance and safeguarding of customer funds?
The Regulation of Financial Services.w: The Electronic Money Directive regulates e-money institutions, covering issuance, safeguarding of funds and capital requirements.

n.0: The Solvency II Directive covers insurers, not e-money firms.
n.2: The UCITS Directive applies to investment funds, not e-money.
n.3: The Bank Recovery and Resolution Directive applies to bank resolution, not e-money.

The Regulation of Financial Services.q: Which EU directive sets the regulatory standards for payment institutions and electronic money firms?
The Regulation of Financial Services.w: The Payment Services Directive sets standards for payment institutions and e-money firms, encouraging innovation and consumer protection.

n.0: The Solvency II Directive applies to insurers, not payment firms.
n.1: The MiFID II Directive governs investment firms, not payments.
n.2: The Bank Recovery and Resolution Directive applies to bank resolution, not payments.

The Regulation of Financial Services.q: Which authority has powers to investigate and enforce against unfair contract terms used in consumer finance?
The Regulation of Financial Services.w: The Competition and Markets Authority has powers to investigate and enforce against unfair contract terms, including in consumer finance.

n.1: The Financial Conduct Authority regulates disclosure and conduct, not unfair terms.
n.2: The Prudential Regulation Authority supervises prudential matters, not contracts.
n.3: The Financial Reporting Council oversees reporting, not contract fairness.

The Regulation of Financial Services.q: Which EU regulation significantly strengthened data protection rules affecting how financial firms handle client data?
o: Markets in Financial Instruments Directive II
The Regulation of Financial Services.w: The General Data Protection Regulation imposed strict rules on data handling and privacy, directly affecting financial firms.

n.0: The Markets in Financial Instruments Directive II focuses on markets and investor protection, not data.
n.2: The Solvency II Directive governs insurers' prudential standards, not data.
n.3: The Basel III Framework sets banking capital rules, not data.

The Regulation of Financial Services.q: Which statement about Section 166 FSMA skilled person reviews is accurate?
o: Both the FCA and PRA may require one
Only the FCA may commission such a report
Only the PRA may commission such a report
It applies solely to Main Market listed issuers
The Regulation of Financial Services.w: Section 166 empowers both the FCA and the PRA to require a firm to appoint a skilled person to report on specified matters.

n.1: The power is shared, not exclusive to the FCA.
n.2: It is not confined to the PRA.
n.3: It applies to authorised firms in scope, not only listed issuers.

The Regulation of Financial Services.q: Which EU directive regulates the management and marketing of alternative investment funds within the EU?
The Regulation of Financial Services.w: The Alternative Investment Fund Managers Directive regulates hedge funds, private equity and other non-UCITS funds marketed in the EU.

n.1: The UCITS Directive governs mutual funds, not alternative funds.
n.2: The MiFID II Directive covers investment services, not alternative funds.
n.3: The Solvency II Directive applies to insurers, not fund managers.

The Regulation of Financial Services.q: Where do the FSMA threshold conditions for authorisation and permission sit?
o: Only in the FCA Handbook’s SUP sourcebook
In statute, applied by the PRA and FCA
Only in the PRA Rulebook, for all firms
In the Listing Rules, for premium issuers
The Regulation of Financial Services.w: Threshold conditions are set in FSMA and secondary legislation, with distinct conditions applied by the PRA and FCA according to their remits.

n.0: They are grounded in statute, not merely a Handbook procedure.
n.2: The PRA does not hold all conditions for all firms.
n.3: The Listing Rules address issuers, not threshold conditions.

The Regulation of Financial Services.q: Which obligation most directly reflects the FCA’s consumer protection role?
o: Setting countercyclical capital buffers at systemic level
Assessing product value and fair outcomes
Acting as resolution authority for failing banks
Setting the base rate to meet the inflation target
The Regulation of Financial Services.w: The FCA’s consumer protection objective drives requirements on fair value, distribution oversight and avoiding foreseeable harm.

n.0: System-level buffers are set by the FPC.
n.2: Resolution is led by the Bank of England.
n.3: Interest-rate setting is the MPC’s role.

The Regulation of Financial Services.q: What is the primary purpose of the UCITS Directive within the European regulatory framework?
o: Set prudential capital requirements for banks
The Regulation of Financial Services.w: The UCITS Directive provides a harmonised framework for collective investment schemes, enabling cross-border distribution in the EU.

n.0: Bank capital is set by Basel and CRD.
n.1: Insurance solvency is governed by Solvency II.
n.2: Electronic payments are covered by the PSD.

The Regulation of Financial Services.q: Which UK Act consolidated regulation under the FSA before being replaced in 2012?
The Regulation of Financial Services.w: FSMA 2000 consolidated financial regulation under the FSA, later reformed by the Financial Services Act 2012 which created the FCA and PRA.

n.0: The Banking Act 2009 introduced resolution, not unified regulation.
n.1: The Companies Act 2006 covers company law, not regulation.
n.2: The Financial Services (Banking Reform) Act 2013 introduced ring-fencing, not FSA consolidation.

The Regulation of Financial Services.q: At the global level, which organisation promotes investor protection and fair, efficient securities markets?
The Regulation of Financial Services.w: IOSCO promotes global standards for securities regulation, focusing on investor protection, market fairness and systemic risk.

n.0: The Basel Committee on Banking Supervision issues banking standards, not securities regulation.
n.1: The International Monetary Fund promotes stability but not securities regulation.
n.2: The World Bank supports development projects, not securities.

The Regulation of Financial Services.q: Which body oversees the UK’s statutory objectives for prudential regulation?
The Regulation of Financial Services.w: The Prudential Regulation Committee oversees the PRA and its statutory objectives, such as the safety and soundness of firms.

n.0: The FCA Board oversees conduct regulation.
n.1: The Treasury Committee scrutinises regulators but does not oversee the objectives directly.
n.3: The CMA enforces competition law.

The Regulation of Financial Services.q: Which FCA statutory objective ensures consumers get appropriate products and services?
The Regulation of Financial Services.w: The FCA’s consumer protection objective requires markets to deliver products and services that meet consumers’ needs and protect them from harm.

n.0: Market integrity concerns confidence and fairness in markets.
n.2: Financial stability is a Bank of England and FPC focus.
n.3: Inflation control is the MPC’s remit.

The Regulation of Financial Services.q: How does HM Treasury exercise control over financial regulation during systemic crises?
o: Through direction powers over the regulators
By setting consumer redress schemes directly
By intervening in routine enforcement cases
By determining individual firms’ capital plans
The Regulation of Financial Services.w: In systemic crises HM Treasury may use direction powers over the Bank of England or regulators, particularly where public funds or resolution tools are involved.

n.1: Redress schemes arise under FCA or FSCS frameworks.
n.2: Routine enforcement remains regulator-led.
n.3: Capital plans are prudential regulator decisions.

The Regulation of Financial Services.q: At the international level, which standards guide insurers' approach to solvency and risk management?
The Regulation of Financial Services.w: The International Association of Insurance Supervisors issues Insurance Core Principles, giving global standards for insurer solvency and risk.

n.0: The Basel III Framework applies to banks, not insurers.
n.1: The MiFID II Directive regulates investment firms, not insurers.
n.2: The OECD Corporate Governance Principles relate to governance, not solvency.

The Regulation of Financial Services.q: Which EU-wide regulation governs the data protection standards financial firms must apply to client data?
The Regulation of Financial Services.w: The GDPR established uniform data protection standards across the EU, with significant implications for financial firms handling client data.

n.0: The MiFID II Directive regulates markets, not data privacy.
n.2: The Solvency II Directive sets insurer solvency standards, not data.
n.3: The UCITS Directive governs collective funds, not data.

The Regulation of Financial Services.q: Which body regulates the professional conduct of solicitors in England and Wales?
The Regulation of Financial Services.w: The Solicitors Regulation Authority regulates solicitors in England and Wales, ensuring high professional standards.

n.0: The Bar Standards Board regulates barristers, not solicitors.
n.1: The Financial Conduct Authority regulates financial firms, not the legal profession.
n.2: The Competition and Markets Authority enforces competition law, not solicitor conduct.

The Regulation of Financial Services.q: Within the UK, which body is responsible for investigating cartel activity that involves banks?
The Regulation of Financial Services.w: The CMA investigates and enforces against anti-competitive practices such as cartels, including in banking markets.

n.0: The Financial Conduct Authority regulates conduct but does not enforce cartels.
n.2: The Prudential Regulation Authority supervises prudential soundness, not competition.
n.3: The Serious Fraud Office prosecutes fraud and corruption, not cartels.

The Regulation of Financial Services.q: Which professional body sets the professional and ethical standards required of chartered accountants in England and Wales?
o: Institute of Chartered Accountants in England and Wales
The Regulation of Financial Services.w: The ICAEW is the professional body that sets ethical and professional standards for its members in the accountancy profession.

n.0: The Financial Reporting Council oversees audit quality but ICAEW sets member standards.
n.1: The Financial Conduct Authority regulates financial conduct, not accountancy.
n.2: The Competition and Markets Authority enforces competition, not professional standards.

The Regulation of Financial Services.q: Which regulator takes enforcement action on data protection breaches that affect consumers' credit reference records?
The Regulation of Financial Services.w: The Information Commissioner's Office enforces data protection law across sectors, including misuse of consumer credit records.

n.1: The Financial Conduct Authority regulates conduct, not data protection breaches.
n.2: The Prudential Regulation Authority focuses on prudential safety, not data.
n.3: The Competition and Markets Authority enforces competition law, not data protection.

The Regulation of Financial Services.q: Which body is responsible for investigating serious and complex fraud that affects UK financial markets?
The Regulation of Financial Services.w: The Serious Fraud Office investigates serious and complex fraud, including cases that affect UK financial markets.

n.0: The Financial Conduct Authority investigates conduct breaches, not complex fraud.
n.2: The Competition and Markets Authority focuses on competition, not fraud.
n.3: The Financial Reporting Council oversees reporting and audit, not fraud.

The Regulation of Financial Services.q: Which EU regulation governs the registration and conduct of credit rating agencies operating in Europe?
The Regulation of Financial Services.w: The Credit Rating Agencies Regulation introduced oversight of rating agencies, requiring registration and conduct standards.

n.0: The MiFID II Directive regulates investment services, not rating agencies.
n.1: The Solvency II Directive applies to insurers, not rating agencies.
n.3: The UCITS Directive applies to investment funds, not rating agencies.

The Regulation of Financial Services.q: What is the Bank of England’s role for payment systems under the Banking Act 2009?
o: Imposing conduct fines on payment providers
Setting statutory minimum fees for payments
The Regulation of Financial Services.w: The Bank of England recognises and supervises systemically important payment systems, ensuring resilience and stability in UK infrastructure.

n.0: Conduct fines fall within the FCA’s remit.
n.1: The Bank does not set minimum fees.
n.2: Product design approval is not part of its remit.

The Regulation of Financial Services.q: Which EU directive created harmonised standards for the recovery and resolution of failing banks?
The Regulation of Financial Services.w: The BRRD sets harmonised EU standards for bank recovery and resolution, ensuring consistency in managing failing banks.

n.0: The MiFID II Directive regulates market conduct, not bank resolution.
n.1: The UCITS Directive applies to funds, not banks.
n.3: The Payment Services Directive regulates payments, not resolution.

The Regulation of Financial Services.q: When is HM Treasury most likely to issue strategic recommendations to the FCA?
The Regulation of Financial Services.w: HM Treasury issues recommendations on strategic priorities, particularly when the regulator’s objectives are updated by legislation.

n.0: An enforcement case is operational FCA business.
n.2: Interest-rate decisions are for the MPC.
n.3: IPO timetables are routine market operations.

The Regulation of Financial Services.q: Which EU directive created a single passport for investment firms across member states?
The Regulation of Financial Services.w: MiFID established the passport allowing investment firms authorised in one EU state to operate across others without separate licences.

n.1: The Solvency II Directive focuses on insurers' capital, not passports.
n.2: The Bank Recovery and Resolution Directive concerns bank recovery, not cross-border services.
n.3: The Payment Services Directive regulates payments, not investment services.

The Regulation of Financial Services.q: Which UK legislation formally established the Financial Policy Committee within the Bank of England?
The Regulation of Financial Services.w: The Financial Services Act 2012 established the FPC within the Bank of England, tasked with macroprudential oversight.

n.0: The Banking Act 2009 created resolution powers, not the FPC.
n.2: The Companies Act 2006 covers corporate law, not central banking.
n.3: The Financial Services and Markets Act 2000 underpins regulation but did not create the FPC.

The Regulation of Financial Services.q: Within the UK, which body is responsible for enforcing advertising standards across broadcast media?
The Regulation of Financial Services.w: Ofcom regulates broadcast media and, alongside the ASA, enforces advertising standards in TV and radio.

n.1: The Advertising Standards Authority covers non-broadcast advertising, not broadcast.
n.2: The Financial Conduct Authority regulates financial promotions, not broadcast ads.
n.3: The Competition and Markets Authority enforces competition, not broadcast advertising.

The Regulation of Financial Services.q: Where does the legal authority for UK monetary policy decisions sit?
o: With the Financial Conduct Authority Board
With the Bank of England’s MPC
The Regulation of Financial Services.w: The Monetary Policy Committee within the Bank of England holds statutory authority for monetary policy decisions.

n.0: HM Treasury sets the framework and accountability, not the decisions.
n.1: The FCA oversees conduct, not monetary policy.
n.3: The DMO manages debt issuance.

The Regulation of Financial Services.q: Which statement best describes HM Treasury’s accountability to Parliament?
o: It is accountable for the regulatory framework
It is responsible for the daily supervision of firms
It decides every enforcement investigation outcome
The Regulation of Financial Services.w: HM Treasury is accountable to Parliament for the statutory and policy framework governing financial regulation.

n.1: Day-to-day supervision is handled by the FCA and PRA.
n.2: Fines are imposed by regulators.
n.3: Enforcement outcomes are decided by regulators.

The Regulation of Financial Services.q: What is the main responsibility of the Prudential Regulation Authority?
The Regulation of Financial Services.w: The PRA’s main responsibility is to promote the safety and soundness of banks, insurers and major investment firms.

n.0: Protecting consumers from promotions is an FCA role.
n.1: National economic policy is managed by HM Treasury.
n.3: Prospectus approval is the FCA’s role.

The Regulation of Financial Services.q: Why might the FCA deploy temporary product intervention rules?
o: To help meet the inflation target quickly
To finance the government’s borrowing requirement
To prevent likely significant consumer detriment
The Regulation of Financial Services.w: The FCA can intervene temporarily where a product poses a serious risk of consumer harm.

n.0: Inflation targeting is for the MPC.
n.1: Systemic liquidity is handled by the Bank of England.
n.2: Borrowing requirements are Treasury matters.

The Regulation of Financial Services.q: Which EU directive regulates payment service providers such as fintechs offering open banking services?
The Regulation of Financial Services.w: PSD2 regulates payment services and introduced open banking, requiring banks and fintechs to give third parties access to payment accounts.

n.0: The MiFID II Directive governs investment firms, not payment providers.
n.1: The UCITS Directive regulates funds, not payments.
n.2: The Solvency II Directive applies to insurers, not payments.

The Regulation of Financial Services.q: Which UK Act enhanced the accountability of the Bank of England after the 2008 crisis?
The Regulation of Financial Services.w: The Financial Services Act 2012 restructured regulation post-crisis, increasing Bank of England accountability and creating the FCA and PRA.

n.0: The Banking Act 2009 introduced resolution tools, not FCA/PRA.
n.2: The Companies Act 2006 is corporate law, not financial regulation.
n.3: The Financial Services and Markets Act 2000 is the original framework, later reformed in 2012.

The Regulation of Financial Services.q: Under the UK’s twin-peaks model, which statement best describes the FCA/PRA split?
o: Both share equal conduct duties for all firms
The PRA handles market abuse; the FCA handles capital
The FCA leads conduct; the PRA leads prudential
The PRA authorises all firms; the FCA supervises all firms
The Regulation of Financial Services.w: The FCA regulates conduct across the market while the PRA handles prudential regulation for banks, building societies and insurers; many large firms are dual-regulated.

n.0: Conduct is not shared equally; the FCA is the conduct regulator.
n.1: Market abuse sits with the FCA and prudential capital with the PRA.
n.3: Authorisation is split, not solely the PRA’s.

The Regulation of Financial Services.q: What did the Markets in Financial Instruments Directive (MiFID II) aim to enhance?
The Regulation of Financial Services.w: MiFID II aimed to improve market transparency, strengthen investor protection and increase competition in EU financial markets.

n.1: Monetary stability is a central-bank matter, not MiFID II.
n.2: Debt issuance is a government and DMO matter.
n.3: Pension funding falls under pensions legislation.

The Regulation of Financial Services.q: Who sets the UK countercyclical capital buffer?
The Regulation of Financial Services.w: The Financial Policy Committee sets the countercyclical capital buffer to address system-wide risk.

n.0: The PRA supervises firms’ safety and soundness, not the macro buffer.
n.1: The MPC sets interest rates for inflation control.
n.2: The FCA focuses on conduct and market integrity.

The Regulation of Financial Services.q: Which body oversees the content of financial promotions appearing in non-broadcast advertising such as press and online?
The Regulation of Financial Services.w: The Advertising Standards Authority regulates advertising content, including financial promotions, ensuring they are not misleading.

n.1: The Financial Conduct Authority regulates conduct but works alongside the ASA on ads.
n.2: The Prudential Regulation Authority supervises prudential risks, not advertising.
n.3: The Competition and Markets Authority enforces competition law, not advertising content.

Financial Regulators’ Responsibilities.q: Why does the FCA’s competition objective explicitly refer to the interests of consumers?
o: To limit the PRA's prudential oversight
To let the FCA set fiscal policy
Financial Regulators’ Responsibilities.w: Framing competition around consumers ensures it promotes innovation, choice and fair pricing for end-users.

n.0: Profitability is not a regulatory aim.
n.1: FCA objectives do not restrict the PRA's role.
n.3: Fiscal policy is HM Treasury's remit.

Financial Regulators’ Responsibilities.q: Which regulator is directly accountable to Parliament for its statutory objectives?
o: Both the FCA and the PRA
Financial Regulators’ Responsibilities.w: Both the FCA and PRA are independent regulators accountable to Parliament for achieving their statutory objectives.

n.0: The PRA is also accountable, not just the FCA.
n.1: The FCA is also accountable.
n.2: Accountability extends to the PRA and FCA separately.

Financial Regulators’ Responsibilities.q: Which PRA principle requires firms to conduct business in a prudent manner?
Financial Regulators’ Responsibilities.w: The PRA requires firms to act in a prudent manner, consistent with promoting safety and soundness.

n.0: Consumer protection is an FCA objective.
n.1: Competition is a secondary PRA objective, not a prudence principle.
n.3: Market integrity is an FCA objective.

Financial Regulators’ Responsibilities.q: Which PRA Fundamental Rule requires firms to prepare for orderly resolution if they fail?
Financial Regulators’ Responsibilities.w: Fundamental Rule 8 obliges firms to prepare for resolution so that, if they fail, the process is orderly and systemic risk is minimised.

n.1: Fundamental Rule 2 is about diligence.
n.2: Fundamental Rule 3 concerns prudence.
n.3: Fundamental Rule 5 deals with risk management.

Financial Regulators’ Responsibilities.q: Which FCA operational objective aims to secure an appropriate degree of protection for consumers?
Financial Regulators’ Responsibilities.w: The consumer protection objective requires the FCA to secure an appropriate degree of protection for consumers.

n.1: Market integrity concerns confidence in markets, not consumer safeguards.
n.2: Competition promotes choice, not direct consumer protection.
n.3: Prudential regulation is the PRA's remit.

Financial Regulators’ Responsibilities.q: Which FCA Principle is most relevant when a firm provides unsuitable advice to retail clients?
Financial Regulators’ Responsibilities.w: Principle 9 requires firms to take reasonable care to ensure the suitability of advice and discretionary decisions.

n.0: Principle 3 concerns organisation and control, not suitability.
n.2: Principle 5 covers market conduct, not suitability.
n.3: Principle 11 concerns regulators, not advice suitability.

Financial Regulators’ Responsibilities.q: Which PRA rule requires firms to have adequate financial resources?
Financial Regulators’ Responsibilities.w: PRA Fundamental Rule 4 requires firms to maintain adequate financial resources to promote safety and soundness.

n.1: Principle 6 is an FCA principle on treating customers fairly.
n.2: COBS 2.1 requires acting honestly and fairly.
n.3: DISP 1.1 relates to complaints handling.

Financial Regulators’ Responsibilities.q: Which FCA operational objective is most closely linked to reducing the risk of market abuse?
Financial Regulators’ Responsibilities.w: The market integrity objective protects and enhances confidence in the UK financial system, including reducing market abuse.

n.0: Consumer protection safeguards individuals.
n.2: Competition promotes choice, not abuse reduction.
n.3: Policyholder protection is a PRA insurance objective.

Financial Regulators’ Responsibilities.q: Which PRA Fundamental Rule requires firms to maintain adequate financial and non-financial resources?
Financial Regulators’ Responsibilities.w: PRA Fundamental Rule 4 requires firms to maintain adequate financial and non-financial resources.

n.1: Fundamental Rule 2 covers skill, care and diligence.
n.2: Fundamental Rule 5 requires sound risk strategies.
n.3: Fundamental Rule 6 relates to organisation and control.

Financial Regulators’ Responsibilities.q: Which FCA sourcebook contains detailed rules about client categorisation?
Financial Regulators’ Responsibilities.w: The Conduct of Business Sourcebook (COBS) contains FCA rules on client categorisation: retail, professional and eligible counterparties.

n.0: CASS deals with client assets.
n.2: DISP covers complaints.
n.3: SYSC sets systems and controls standards.

Financial Regulators’ Responsibilities.q: Which FCA sanction requires firms to repay customers who suffered loss?
Financial Regulators’ Responsibilities.w: Restitution orders require firms to return money to customers harmed by misconduct.

n.0: Public censure affects reputation, not compensation.
n.1: Prohibition orders ban individuals, not provide compensation.
n.3: Decision notices confirm action, not redress.

Financial Regulators’ Responsibilities.q: Which authority is primarily responsible for prosecuting insider dealing offences?
Financial Regulators’ Responsibilities.w: The FCA investigates insider dealing, but prosecutions are usually brought by the Crown Prosecution Service under the CJA 1993.

n.0: The FCA refers serious criminal cases rather than prosecuting.
n.1: The PRA handles prudential regulation, not prosecutions.
n.3: The Bank of England manages monetary policy, not prosecutions.

Financial Regulators’ Responsibilities.q: Which sanction is available under both FCA enforcement and criminal law?
Financial Regulators’ Responsibilities.w: Financial penalties can be applied by the FCA under civil enforcement and by courts under criminal proceedings.

n.1: Public censure is a regulatory sanction only.
n.2: Restitution is an FCA civil remedy, not criminal.
n.3: Supervision notices are not sanctions.

Financial Regulators’ Responsibilities.q: What is the maximum criminal penalty for insider dealing under the Criminal Justice Act 1993?
o: Up to two years and a capped fine
A lifetime ban from all regulated activities
Up to seven years and an unlimited fine
Only civil financial penalties, no imprisonment
Financial Regulators’ Responsibilities.w: Insider dealing under the CJA 1993 carries a maximum of seven years' imprisonment and/or an unlimited fine.

n.0: This understates the statutory maximum penalty.
n.1: A ban is a regulatory sanction, not the criminal maximum.
n.3: Criminal penalties exist under statute, not just civil fines.

Financial Regulators’ Responsibilities.q: What is the purpose of a restitution order under FCA enforcement?
o: To compensate customers for losses from misconduct
To publicise a firm's misconduct openly
To bar an individual from all regulated activities
Financial Regulators’ Responsibilities.w: Restitution orders require firms to compensate affected clients for financial losses caused by misconduct.

n.1: Publicising breaches is done via censure or final notices.
n.2: Barring individuals is a prohibition order.
n.3: Suspension is a separate regulatory sanction.

Financial Regulators’ Responsibilities.q: What is the FCA’s single strategic objective under FSMA?
o: To maximise profits for UK firms
To ensure relevant markets function well
Financial Regulators’ Responsibilities.w: The FCA's strategic objective is to ensure relevant markets function well, supported by three operational objectives.

n.0: Profitability is not a regulatory objective.
n.1: Zero complaints is unrealistic and not statutory.
n.3: Monetary stability is the Bank of England's role.

Financial Regulators’ Responsibilities.q: Which statutory objective guides the PRA when dealing with insurers?
Financial Regulators’ Responsibilities.w: The PRA has a specific insurance objective: to contribute to securing an appropriate degree of protection for policyholders.

n.1: Consumer protection is an FCA objective.
n.2: Competition is not a PRA primary objective.
n.3: Market integrity belongs to the FCA.

Financial Regulators’ Responsibilities.q: Which PRA Fundamental Rule requires firms to conduct business with integrity?
Financial Regulators’ Responsibilities.w: PRA Fundamental Rule 1 requires firms to conduct business with integrity, underpinning all other prudential obligations.

n.0: Fundamental Rule 3 requires acting prudently.
n.1: Fundamental Rule 5 requires effective risk strategies.
n.3: Fundamental Rule 6 relates to organisation and control.

Financial Regulators’ Responsibilities.q: Which FCA objective is particularly relevant to ensuring firms communicate clearly with retail clients?
Financial Regulators’ Responsibilities.w: The consumer protection objective requires an appropriate degree of protection for consumers, including clear and fair communication.

n.0: Market integrity concerns system confidence.
n.1: Competition promotes choice.
n.2: Monetary stability is unrelated to communications.

Financial Regulators’ Responsibilities.q: Which piece of legislation criminalises misleading statements and practices in financial markets?
Financial Regulators’ Responsibilities.w: The Financial Services Act 2012 created criminal offences for misleading statements and market manipulation.

n.0: The Companies Act governs company law, not market offences.
n.2: The Consumer Rights Act covers consumer contracts.
n.3: The CJA 1993 focuses on insider dealing.

Financial Regulators’ Responsibilities.q: What disciplinary tool can the FCA use to deter misconduct without imposing a financial penalty?
Financial Regulators’ Responsibilities.w: Public censure publishes details of a breach, damaging reputation as a deterrent without a financial penalty.

n.0: A prohibition order bans individuals, not purely reputational.
n.1: Injunctions stop behaviour, not primarily reputational.
n.2: Restitution orders require redress, not reputational harm.

Financial Regulators’ Responsibilities.q: Which PRA Fundamental Rule requires firms to have sound risk strategies and risk management systems?
Financial Regulators’ Responsibilities.w: PRA Fundamental Rule 5 requires firms to have effective risk strategies and risk management systems appropriate to their business.

n.1: Fundamental Rule 2 requires skill, care and diligence.
n.2: Fundamental Rule 3 requires prudence.
n.3: Fundamental Rule 6 concerns organisation and control.

Financial Regulators’ Responsibilities.q: Which PRA Fundamental Rule requires firms to conduct their business with due skill, care, and diligence?
Financial Regulators’ Responsibilities.w: PRA Fundamental Rule 2 requires firms to conduct business with due skill, care and diligence.

n.0: Fundamental Rule 1 covers integrity.
n.1: Fundamental Rule 3 concerns prudence.
n.3: Fundamental Rule 4 relates to adequate resources.

Financial Regulators’ Responsibilities.q: Which of the following is a criminal offence under FSMA 2000?
o: Carrying on regulated activities without authorisation
Failing to answer a complaint within eight weeks
Publishing a promotion that is misleading
Financial Regulators’ Responsibilities.w: Carrying on regulated activities without authorisation is a criminal offence under FSMA 2000, punishable by fine and imprisonment.

n.1: Complaint deadlines are FCA rules, not criminal law.
n.2: Misleading promotions are not always criminal.
n.3: Resource breaches attract regulatory penalties, not crime.

Financial Regulators’ Responsibilities.q: Which of the following is one of the FCA’s three operational objectives?
Financial Regulators’ Responsibilities.w: One of the FCA's operational objectives is to protect and enhance the integrity of the UK financial system.

n.0: Fiscal policy is set by HM Treasury.
n.1: Payments infrastructure oversight sits with the Bank of England.
n.3: Interest rates are set by the MPC.

Financial Regulators’ Responsibilities.q: Which PRA Fundamental Rule requires firms to deal fairly with their policyholders?
Financial Regulators’ Responsibilities.w: Fundamental Rule 6 requires firms to organise and control their affairs responsibly, which extends to dealing fairly with policyholders.

n.0: Fundamental Rule 1 requires integrity, not fair treatment directly.
n.1: Fundamental Rule 2 concerns diligence, not fairness.
n.3: Fundamental Rule 5 relates to risk systems, not fairness.

Financial Regulators’ Responsibilities.q: Which enforcement outcome is published to ensure transparency and deterrence?
Financial Regulators’ Responsibilities.w: Final notices are published by the FCA to provide transparency about enforcement action and to deter misconduct.

n.1: Warning notices are not published in full.
n.2: Decision notices are usually confidential pending appeal.
n.3: Restitution orders are redress, not a transparency tool.

Financial Regulators’ Responsibilities.q: Which body has the power to prosecute criminal insider dealing cases in the UK?
Financial Regulators’ Responsibilities.w: The FCA investigates insider dealing, but criminal prosecutions are brought by the Crown Prosecution Service under the CJA 1993.

n.0: The FCA usually refers serious criminal cases rather than prosecuting.
n.2: The PRA is a prudential regulator, not a prosecutor.
n.3: The CMA deals with competition law, not insider dealing.

Financial Regulators’ Responsibilities.q: Which FCA enforcement action involves requiring a firm to cease certain business activities immediately?
Financial Regulators’ Responsibilities.w: The FCA can vary or withdraw a firm's permission, requiring it to stop certain regulated activities immediately.

n.0: Public censure exposes misconduct but does not restrict permissions.
n.2: Final notices confirm completed action, not immediate restrictions.
n.3: Thematic reviews assess sector practice, not individual restrictions.

Financial Regulators’ Responsibilities.q: Which regulator applies a judgement-led, forward-looking approach to supervision of systemic firms?
Financial Regulators’ Responsibilities.w: The PRA uses a judgement-led, forward-looking approach to supervise firms whose failure would affect stability.

n.0: The FCA supervises conduct, not prudential systemic risk.
n.2: The SFO prosecutes fraud.
n.3: The FOS resolves complaints.

Financial Regulators’ Responsibilities.q: What is the maximum fine the FCA can impose for breaches of its rules?
Financial Regulators’ Responsibilities.w: The FCA can impose unlimited financial penalties, with the amount reflecting the seriousness and impact of the breach.

n.0: Penalties can exceed £1 million.
n.1: £10 million is below possible fines for serious breaches.
n.2: £50 million is not a statutory cap.

Financial Regulators’ Responsibilities.q: Which FCA enforcement measure focuses on restoring consumers financially after harm?
Financial Regulators’ Responsibilities.w: Restitution orders compel firms to compensate consumers who suffered financial loss due to misconduct.

n.0: Public censure addresses reputation, not compensation.
n.1: Prohibition orders ban individuals, not provide redress.
n.2: Warning notices outline proposed action, not restitution.

Financial Regulators’ Responsibilities.q: Which body has powers to investigate and prosecute serious fraud in addition to FCA enforcement?
Financial Regulators’ Responsibilities.w: The Serious Fraud Office investigates and prosecutes serious or complex fraud, complementing the FCA's enforcement remit.

n.0: The FOS resolves complaints, not fraud prosecutions.
n.2: The PRA supervises prudential safety, not fraud.
n.3: The CMA oversees competition law, not fraud.

Financial Regulators’ Responsibilities.q: Which PRA objective ensures it supervises banks to reduce systemic risk?
Financial Regulators’ Responsibilities.w: The PRA's primary safety and soundness objective ensures banks and investment firms are supervised to limit systemic risk.

n.0: Consumer protection is an FCA objective.
n.2: Market integrity belongs to the FCA.
n.3: Competition is only a secondary PRA objective.

Financial Regulators’ Responsibilities.q: Which PRA Fundamental Rule requires firms to maintain effective information systems for regulators?
Financial Regulators’ Responsibilities.w: PRA Fundamental Rule 7 requires firms to deal openly with regulators and provide information as reasonably required.

n.0: Fundamental Rule 1 covers integrity.
n.1: Fundamental Rule 4 covers resources.
n.3: Fundamental Rule 5 deals with risk systems.

Financial Regulators’ Responsibilities.q: How does the FCA use thematic reviews within its supervisory approach?
o: To review only firms reporting poor results
To assess risks across a whole sector
To investigate only firms in insolvency
To review fiscal policy for HM Treasury
Financial Regulators’ Responsibilities.w: Thematic reviews assess practices and risks across a whole sector or product type rather than a single firm.

n.0: Poor performance alone does not trigger a thematic review.
n.2: Insolvency investigations are separate from thematic reviews.
n.3: Fiscal policy is the Treasury's role, not the FCA's.

Financial Regulators’ Responsibilities.q: Which PRA Fundamental Rule requires firms to prepare for resolution?
Financial Regulators’ Responsibilities.w: Fundamental Rule 8 requires PRA-regulated firms to prepare for resolution so that failure can occur in an orderly way.

n.1: Fundamental Rule 1 requires integrity.
n.2: Fundamental Rule 4 concerns adequate resources.
n.3: Fundamental Rule 6 concerns organisation and control.

Financial Regulators’ Responsibilities.q: Which PRA Fundamental Rule requires firms to act in a prudent manner?
Financial Regulators’ Responsibilities.w: PRA Fundamental Rule 3 requires firms to act in a prudent manner, consistent with safety and soundness.

n.1: Fundamental Rule 1 covers integrity.
n.2: Fundamental Rule 2 covers diligence.
n.3: Fundamental Rule 5 relates to risk systems.

Financial Regulators’ Responsibilities.q: Which FCA notice is the final public record of enforcement action taken?
Financial Regulators’ Responsibilities.w: A final notice is published to record the FCA's enforcement decision once appeal processes are complete.

n.0: Decision notices precede final notices and may be appealed.
n.1: Warning notices are earlier in the process.
n.2: Injunctions stop behaviour but are not notices.

Financial Regulators’ Responsibilities.q: What is the relationship between the PRA and the FCA in delivering statutory objectives?
o: They compete directly for regulatory authority
They have distinct remits but coordinate
They are both overseen by the MPC
Financial Regulators’ Responsibilities.w: The PRA and FCA have complementary but distinct objectives, prudential versus conduct, and coordinate closely.

n.0: They cooperate, not compete.
n.1: Their objectives differ.
n.3: The MPC sets monetary policy, not oversight of them.

Financial Regulators’ Responsibilities.q: Which UK authority investigates and prosecutes serious fraud cases involving financial services?
Financial Regulators’ Responsibilities.w: The Serious Fraud Office investigates and prosecutes complex and serious fraud, often working alongside the FCA.

n.0: The FCA often refers complex fraud cases to the SFO.
n.1: The PRA manages prudential risk, not prosecutions.
n.3: The FOS handles complaints, not prosecutions.

Financial Regulators’ Responsibilities.q: Which FCA principle requires firms to deal with regulators in an open and cooperative way?
Financial Regulators’ Responsibilities.w: Principle 11 requires firms to deal with regulators openly and cooperatively and disclose anything they would reasonably expect.

n.0: Principle 2 relates to skill, care and diligence.
n.1: Principle 4 covers financial resources.
n.2: Principle 7 covers clear client communications.

Financial Regulators’ Responsibilities.q: What is the purpose of risk-based supervision by the PRA?
o: To supervise only the smallest retail-focused firms
To review firms only once insolvency occurs
To focus on firms threatening financial stability
To enforce competition law across all sectors
Financial Regulators’ Responsibilities.w: The PRA targets firms whose disorderly failure would harm financial stability, allocating supervisory intensity accordingly.

n.0: Both retail and wholesale firms are supervised by systemic risk.
n.1: Supervision is proactive, not limited to post-failure.
n.3: Competition law is the CMA's remit, not the PRA's.

Financial Regulators’ Responsibilities.q: Which body oversees the FCA and PRA in setting their statutory objectives?
Financial Regulators’ Responsibilities.w: HM Treasury sets the legislative and policy framework within which the FCA and PRA operate.

n.1: The CMA enforces general competition law.
n.2: The FOS resolves complaints.
n.3: The PSR regulates payments infrastructure.

Financial Regulators’ Responsibilities.q: Which FCA principle requires firms to conduct their business with due skill, care and diligence?
Financial Regulators’ Responsibilities.w: Principle 2 obliges firms to conduct their business with due skill, care and diligence.

n.0: Principle 1 relates to integrity.
n.1: Principle 3 covers organisation and risk systems.
n.2: Principle 5 relates to market conduct.

Financial Regulators’ Responsibilities.q: Which FCA notice is issued first in the enforcement process?
Financial Regulators’ Responsibilities.w: A warning notice is the first formal step, setting out proposed action and allowing representations.

n.0: Decision notices follow warning notices.
n.2: Final notices come at the end of the process.
n.3: Restitution orders are remedies, not initial notices.

Financial Regulators’ Responsibilities.q: Which FCA principle is most relevant to ensuring that financial promotions are fair and not misleading?
Financial Regulators’ Responsibilities.w: Principle 7 requires clear, fair and not misleading communications with clients, covering financial promotions.

n.0: Principle 2 covers diligence.
n.2: Principle 4 concerns resources.
n.3: Principle 9 relates to suitability of advice.

Financial Regulators’ Responsibilities.q: Which FCA principle requires firms to conduct their business with integrity?
Financial Regulators’ Responsibilities.w: Principle 1 requires firms to conduct business with integrity, the foundation of the FCA's principles-based regime.

n.0: Principle 2 is about diligence.
n.2: Principle 4 covers financial resources.
n.3: Principle 6 covers treating customers fairly.

Financial Regulators’ Responsibilities.q: Which regulator has a secondary competition objective when advancing its primary objectives?
Financial Regulators’ Responsibilities.w: The PRA has a secondary competition objective, facilitating effective competition when advancing safety and soundness.

n.1: The FCA has competition as a primary objective.
n.2: The FOS resolves complaints.
n.3: HM Treasury sets policy, not a statutory competition objective here.

Financial Regulators’ Responsibilities.q: Which FCA operational objective is intended to ensure trust and resilience in financial markets?
Financial Regulators’ Responsibilities.w: The market integrity objective maintains trust, resilience and transparency in financial markets.

n.0: Consumer protection concerns individual safeguards.
n.2: Competition fosters choice.
n.3: The secondary competition objective belongs to the PRA.

Financial Regulators’ Responsibilities.q: Which FCA Principle requires a firm to manage conflicts of interest fairly?
Financial Regulators’ Responsibilities.w: Principle 8 requires firms to manage conflicts of interest fairly, both between the firm and its clients and between one client and another.

n.1: Principle 2 concerns skill and diligence, not conflicts.
n.2: Principle 3 covers organisation and control, not conflicts.
n.3: Principle 7 covers client communications, not conflicts.

Financial Regulators’ Responsibilities.q: How do the PRA and FCA avoid duplication while fulfilling their statutory objectives?
o: By focusing on distinct areas and coordinating
By competing for authority over firms
By setting identical statutory objectives for both
By merging into a single regulator
Financial Regulators’ Responsibilities.w: The FCA covers conduct and competition and the PRA prudential soundness; coordination prevents overlap.

n.1: They cooperate, not compete.
n.2: Their objectives differ.
n.3: They remain separate regulators.

Financial Regulators’ Responsibilities.q: Which sanction allows the FCA to ban individuals from carrying out regulated activities?
Financial Regulators’ Responsibilities.w: A prohibition order prevents an unfit individual from carrying out regulated activities, permanently or temporarily.

n.0: Public censure is reputational, not a ban.
n.1: Restitution orders require compensation, not bans.
n.3: Advisory notices give guidance, not enforceable sanctions.

Financial Regulators’ Responsibilities.q: Which regulator supervises anti-money laundering systems and controls in UK financial firms?
Financial Regulators’ Responsibilities.w: The FCA supervises anti-money laundering systems and controls in firms under the Money Laundering Regulations 2017.

n.1: The PRA's remit is prudential soundness, not AML.
n.2: The Bank of England focuses on financial stability.
n.3: The CMA enforces competition law, not AML.

Financial Regulators’ Responsibilities.q: Which PRA Fundamental Rule requires firms to deal with regulators in an open and cooperative way?
Financial Regulators’ Responsibilities.w: PRA Fundamental Rule 7 requires firms to deal with regulators openly and cooperatively and disclose information appropriately.

n.0: Fundamental Rule 1 requires integrity.
n.1: Fundamental Rule 3 requires prudence.
n.3: Fundamental Rule 5 concerns risk strategies.

Financial Regulators’ Responsibilities.q: Which PRA Fundamental Rule requires firms to act with integrity?
Financial Regulators’ Responsibilities.w: Fundamental Rule 1 requires firms to conduct their business with integrity.

n.0: Fundamental Rule 2 requires diligence, not integrity.
n.2: Fundamental Rule 3 concerns prudence, not integrity.
n.3: Fundamental Rule 6 covers organisation and control, not integrity.

Financial Regulators’ Responsibilities.q: Which UK Act introduced criminal offences for misleading statements in financial markets?
Financial Regulators’ Responsibilities.w: The Financial Services Act 2012 introduced new criminal offences for misleading statements and practices in markets.

n.0: The CJA 1993 focuses on insider dealing.
n.2: The Companies Act concerns company law.
n.3: The Banking Act addresses bank resolution.

Financial Regulators’ Responsibilities.q: Under FSMA, what is the FCA’s strategic objective?
Financial Regulators’ Responsibilities.w: FSMA sets the FCA's strategic objective as ensuring that relevant markets function well.

n.0: Profitability is not a statutory objective.
n.1: Protection is appropriate, not absolute, so zero detriment is not the aim.
n.2: Monetary policy is the Bank of England's remit.

Financial Regulators’ Responsibilities.q: Which regulator has the statutory duty to promote effective competition only when advancing its primary objectives?
Financial Regulators’ Responsibilities.w: The PRA has a secondary competition objective, considering competition when advancing its safety and soundness objectives.

n.0: The FCA has competition as a primary objective.
n.2: The CMA enforces general competition law.
n.3: The FOS resolves disputes.

Financial Regulators’ Responsibilities.q: Which notice is issued by the FCA after considering representations and deciding to proceed with enforcement?
Financial Regulators’ Responsibilities.w: A decision notice is issued after representations, setting out the FCA's decision to take enforcement action subject to appeal.

n.0: Warning notices precede decision notices.
n.1: Supervision notices are not part of this process.
n.3: Final notices come after decisions and appeals.

Financial Regulators’ Responsibilities.q: What is the purpose of publishing FCA final notices?
o: To promote transparency and deter misconduct
To serve as the official criminal prosecution records
To notify Parliament of the FCA's budget
Financial Regulators’ Responsibilities.w: Publishing final notices ensures transparency in enforcement and deters misconduct across the market.

n.1: Final notices follow, not replace, decision notices.
n.2: Criminal prosecutions are separate from FCA notices.
n.3: Budget reporting is unrelated to notices.

Financial Regulators’ Responsibilities.q: Which type of FCA enforcement action requires firms to return money to consumers harmed by misconduct?
Financial Regulators’ Responsibilities.w: Restitution orders require firms to compensate consumers who suffered loss due to misconduct.

n.0: Prohibition orders ban individuals, not require repayment.
n.1: Public censure is reputational, not compensatory.
n.2: Warning notices signal proposed action, not repayment.

Financial Regulators’ Responsibilities.q: Which PRA Fundamental Rule requires firms to act with due regard to the safety and soundness of the UK financial system?
